Australian politician fails to overturn racial vilification ruling over telling Muslim senator to go back to Pakistan. A popular far-right Australian politician failed on Monday to overturn a racial vilification finding that was handed down after she told a Muslim senator to go back to Pakistan. Senator Pauline Hanson has emerged as one of Australia’s most popular politicians, wooing voters with calls for strict immigration curbs, mass deportations of “illegal migrants” and enhanced free speech protections. Hanson took aim at Pakistan-born Australian lawmaker Mehreen Faruqi in 2022 over comments made in the wake of Queen Elizabeth II’s death . Faruqi, a left-leaning Greens senator, said she could not mourn the “leader of a racist empire built on stolen lives, land and wealth of colonised people”. Hanson replied on social media: “When you immigrated to Australia you took every advantage of this country. You took citizenship, bought multiple homes, and a job in a parliament. It’s clear you’re not happy, so pack your bags and piss off back to Pakistan.” The Federal Court of Australia found in 2024, in response to a complaint from Faruqi, that Hanson’s comments amounted to a “strong form of racism”. The judge found Hanson’s post breached Australia’s laws against racial discrimination as it was reasonably likely to offend, insult, humiliate and intimidate Faruqi, as well as Muslim Australians and people of colour who had migrated to the country. Hanson appealed the decision, arguing she did not breach the law and the law was in any case constitutionally invalid. Her appeal was dismissed on Monday. “I was incensed by the incredible disrespect that I felt was shown to our late Queen on the day of her death by Senator Faruqi and others,” she said after the court’s decision. “I simply wanted to call that out.” For years a political outsider, Hanson’s One Nation has surged this year to become one of the country’s most popular parties, according to opinion polls. Hanson has pledged sweeping cuts to government spending — akin to Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) in the United States — and has urged Australia to rethink its membership of international organisations.

Mass shooting kills 3, wounds 4 near Space Needle landmark in Seattle. A mass shooting near the Space Needle landmark in Seattle killed three people on Sunday and wounded at least four others, including a toddler, according to the police. Seattle Police said one suspect has been arrested and they are searching for another following the incident at a food festival in a popular tourist district of the northwestern US city. Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis said shots were heard around 6pm (6am PKT) and “there were two people who we believe were shooting at each other”. Two weapons were recovered. There is “no outstanding threat to the community,” he said. Seattle Police said three people had died. Police said on X earlier Sunday there were “multiple shooting victims” after shots were fired at the Seattle Centre. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson said State Patrol SWAT officers had been deployed to assist local police. “My prayers are with the families of the victims, and the responders as they work to keep people safe,” he said on X. Mayor Katie Wilson said the shooting was “an act of horrific violence”. “Our attention belongs to the people whose lives were taken, those fighting to recover, and the families beside them,” she said in a statement. She also expressed her thanks to “the Seattle police officers who responded to the scene and took a suspect into custody.” Four patients were being treated at the trauma centre facility at Harborview Medical Centre, according to spokesperson Susan Gregg: a child, a woman of unknown age who was in surgery, a 23-year-old man and a 39-year-old woman. Davis said those in the hospital were in a “stable condition”. Several witnesses told Seattle television station KIRO they heard multiple shots before running away. “At first, I thought there were fireworks, and then everybody flooded and ran past us,” Nick Bate told the station. “We started running. I didn’t know. I didn’t look where the person was going. I just heard everything,” a witness told AFP. The shooting took place during the “Bite of Seattle” summer festival celebrating local businesses and food vendors.

I’m on an admissions committee and universities need to talk about this. I have worked on my university’s Admission Committee for 16 years, long enough to have watched several cycles of both growth and contraction. But nothing in those years prepared me for what the last three or four have looked like, and nothing about the current decline is evenly spread. It is concentrated, sharply, among girls applying to evening programmes. When I began speaking directly with hesitant applicants and their parents to understand why confirmed seats were being given up, the reasoning was strikingly consistent, and stated without much hesitation. “In this inflation, why should I spend such a heavy amount on my daughter’s education when there is no job security for her in the future?” one mother asked me plainly. With no guaranteed job waiting at the end of an evening degree, she said, that money was better saved for her daughter’s dowry and wedding than spent on tuition. She was not the only parent to put it like that. These were not abstractions to me. They were mothers, often visibly uneasy themselves, explaining a trade-off they felt they had no real choice but to make. Every admission cycle now brings the same quiet moment in our committee meetings: a target intake number that used to be a formality is instead a subject of real concern. Punjab’s Higher Education Department reports admissions down 20 to 30 per cent across many public universities this year, and national enrolment has fallen nearly 12pc, or roughly 262,000 students, since its 2020-21 peak, according to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2025. Sitting on my own university’s admission and financial aid committees, I no longer read those figures as an abstraction. I watch them happen, one hesitant applicant at a time. It is worth pausing on why this trade-off falls so heavily on girls specifically. Evening programmes have long served students, many of them women, who could not attend morning classes because of household responsibilities or affordability, making the evening seat itself already a hard-won compromise. That families are now weighing a daughter’s tuition against her dowry tells us this is no longer only a story about the price of education. It is a story about whose future a stretched household chooses to invest in when it can no longer confidently invest in both, and a reminder that when trust in a degree’s payoff collapses, it is often girls who lose their seat first. Much of the public conversation about this decline reaches for the obvious culprits: inflation, tuition, currency depreciation, a job market that cannot absorb the roughly 445,000 graduates Pakistan produces each year, of whom by some estimates over 31pc remain unemployed. These are real pressures, and they matter. But as someone who has spent 16 years inside a public sector education department, I think the more uncomfortable diagnosis is closer to home: we in higher education have been slow to prove that what we teach is still worth four years of a young person’s life. I say this carefully, because it is not a comfortable thing for an academic to admit. But when I talk to prospective students and their parents, the hesitation is rarely just about money. It is about whether the degree on offer will actually change anything. Families increasingly compare a four-year programme against a six-month coding bootcamp, a freelancing certificate, or simply a plane ticket. Too often, and too honestly, the university does not win that comparison, because our curricula have not moved as fast as the labour market has. This is where I think the profession, including institutions like my own, needs to look inward rather than only outward. Degree programmes across the public sector still largely run on syllabi and delivery methods designed for a different economy. Employers now want demonstrable, specific skills; we are still largely credentialing years completed. Until departments treat curriculum review as a standing, funded obligation rather than an occasional exercise, no amount of scholarship money will fully answer the question families are asking: what, exactly, will this degree let my child do that they could not do otherwise? None of this means the economic pressures are secondary. Over 727,000 Pakistanis left for work abroad in 2024-25 alone, and roughly one in three graduates aged 25 to 35 say they have considered migration. For many households, a local postgraduate degree increasingly looks like a costly detour on the way to an exit visa rather than a necessary step. Addressing that will require targeted, income-linked scholarships and student-loan schemes rather than the thinly spread support most provinces currently offer. But if I had to choose one lever that universities themselves control, and are not pulling hard enough, it is trust. Departments should publish graduate employment outcomes as openly as they publish merit lists. Every programme should be able to show, in plain numbers, what its last three cohorts are doing now. Where that number is uncomfortable, it should drive reform, not silence. Where it is strong, it should be the first thing prospective students see, not an afterthought buried in a prospectus. I do not think the decline in admissions is a temporary dip that will correct itself once inflation eases. It is a verdict, delivered by thousands of individual families doing their own arithmetic on cost, risk, and return. Reversing it will take more than another extended deadline. It will take those of us inside the system proving, programme by programme, that a Pakistani university degree still opens a door worth walking through. Header art created via generative AI

Oil prices dip over 6pc after US, Iran pause fighting over weekend. Oil prices tumbled more than six per cent on Monday after the US and Iran paused strikes over the weekend after two weeks of attacks, raising hopes of a diplomatic solution that would de-escalate the conflict and allow shipping to resume in the Strait of Hormuz . Brent crude futures fell $6.20, or 6.4pc, to $90.58 by 0620 GMT after briefly slipping under the key support level of $90 earlier in the session. US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $83.51 a barrel, down $5.80, or 6.5pc. Both contracts are trading at their lowest levels in nearly a week after rising for the past three weeks. Brent had reached $100 per barrel as the conflict, which reduced oil shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, spilled over to the Red Sea, hindering exports from the world’s top exporter, Saudi Arabia, via the Bab el-Mandeb strait to Asia. The US ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, told Fox News on Sunday and other US media that President Donald Trump had decided to pause US attacks to allow more time for diplomacy. “Oil prices fell sharply in early trading as the US and Iran refrained from further military action, offering the first tangible signs of a potential de-escalation in tensions,” said ING analysts in a client note. “The price action in oil this morning clearly reflects the market’s desperation for positive news.” Despite the pause in attacks, fewer than 10 commodity vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz daily during the weekend, shipping data from Kpler showed. “Any rebound in flows through the Strait of Hormuz is likely to prove slow and partial, as many shippers remain wary and will want greater confidence in their safety before they bring more empty ships into the Strait,” MST Marquee analyst Saul Kavonic said. In addition, ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb strait fell on Sunday after Yemeni Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast, although a third Chinese supertanker exited via Bab el-Mandeb. However, some analysts are still expecting markets to be supported if crude supplies stay affected by ongoing shipping risks in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war. “As the Middle East conflict widened to the Red Sea and Ukrainian drones struck Russian ships and refineries … Sustained (supply) disruption would likely keep oil prices elevated and continue to pose upside risks to global inflation,” said UOB analysts in a note. Ukraine said it hit several Russian oil sites over the weekend.

FO condemns Indian minister's remarks on Kashmir issue, warns against underestimating resolve to thwart 'any adventurism'. The Foreign Office (FO) has condemned Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh’s “highly provocative and irresponsible comments” regarding the Kashmir dispute, saying that the neighbouring country must not underestimate Pakistan’s resolve to “thwart any Indian adventurism”. On Sunday, Singh had stated that there would be “no talks with Pakistan”. According to the Times of India , he went on to say that if any took place, they would only be on Azad Jammu and Kashmir, claiming that it was “illegally occupied by Pakistan”. He also said that any “misadventure” would invite a response “beyond their imagination”, the publication said. The FO responded to the claims in a statement issued early on Monday, saying Pakistan condemned in the “strongest possible terms the highly provocative and irresponsible comments” by the Indian defence minister. “His statement not only distorts facts regarding the UN and internationally recognised Jammu and Kashmir dispute that remains on the agenda of the UN Security Council but also shows Indian government’s deliberate policy to threaten regional and international peace and security,” the FO said. “Such insinuations are an attempt to divert attention from India’s continued occupation of Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, its sponsorship of terrorism across the region, as well as its domestic instability,” it said. “While resorting to its misplaced rhetoric of aggression and belligerence, India must not underestimate the people and government of Pakistan’s unwavering resolve and determination to thwart any Indian adventurism as demonstrated by the entire Pakistani nation and its valiant armed forces during Operation Bunyanum Marsoos last year,” it said. In May 2025, a four-day conflict between Pakistan and India was sparked by an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir, which New Delhi, without evidence, linked with Pakistan. Islamabad strongly denied responsibility while calling for a neutral investigation . The two had traded tit-for-tat strikes before American intervention on May 10 led to a ceasefire . “Pakistan urges the international community, in particular the United Nations, to take note of India’s continued rogue behaviour and to hold it accountable for its failure to uphold the relevant UN Security Council resolutions that guarantee the right to self-determination of the people of Jammu and Kashmir,” the FO statement said. Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said that India’s “continued attempts to rewrite internationally recognised legal realities through coercive rhetoric cannot alter the facts”. Referencing Singh’s remarks, he said that such statements reflected a continued attempt to distort internationally recognised legal realities through political rhetoric and coercive posturing. “They neither alter the status of the Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir nor contribute to regional peace, stability or meaningful dialogue,” the minister said in a post on X. “India’s repeated attempts to malign Pakistan lack credibility in light of its own well-documented record of state-sponsored terrorism and criminal activities. In fact, India remains the biggest sponsor of terrorism and perpetrator of instability in South Asia, holding the region hostage to its aggressively revisionist designs,” Asif said. “Equally alarming is India’s irresponsible rhetoric which risks lowering the threshold for interstate conflict in the region,” he added. Asif said that Pakistan remained committed to peace and dialogue but its resolve to safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security “is absolute and must never be tested”. “Defence minister’s rhetoric is an attempt to deflect the attention from internal turmoil and increasing unrest and discontent against Modi’s autocratic and divisive style of governance,” he said.

First phase of AJK polls underway in Mirpur division amid allegations of rigging. The first phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections is underway in the 13 constituencies of Mirpur division. Polling began at 8am and will continue till 5pm. Today (Monday) has been declared a public holiday in all three districts — Bhimber, Mirpur, and Kotli — of the division to facilitate polling. A total of 288 candidates are contesting today’s election. According to the Election Commission, votes will be cast at 2,316 polling stations, of which 1,241 have been declared “highly sensitive” and 724 “sensitive”. Election monitoring has been organised through 13 zones and 205 sectors across the division, while 18,560 personnel from police and other law enforcement agencies have been deployed under a three-tier security plan. A voter casts his vote at a polling station in Mirpur, Azad Jammu and Kashmir on July 27, in the first phase of general elections in AJK. — Photo provided by author Under the arrangement, police are providing the first layer of security, Pakistan Rangers (Punjab), Pakistan Rangers (Sindh) and the Federal Constabulary the second, and the Pakistan Army the third. Around 2,100 army personnel were also to be deployed, while Quick Response Force teams were to remain on standby to respond to any emergency. Skirmishes and scuffles between workers of the PPP and PML-N were reported in some areas of Kotli district, where both parties have accused the other of rigging at some polling stations. Subsequently, polling at certain stations was briefly suspended before it was allowed to resume. Mirpur Commissioner Raja Tahir Mumtaz Khan visited various polling stations and noted that the electoral process was underway across the division with the “security apparatus in place”. AJK Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan cast his ballot at a polling station in Bhimber’s Samahni tehsil. AJK Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram Khan casts his ballot at a polling station in Bhimber’s Samahni tehsil. — photo via Tariq Naqash Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns. The second and third phases are scheduled for August 2 and August 10 in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies, and 11 constituencies of Poonch division, respectively. Rigging allegations Ahead of the voting, the PML-N alleged pre-poll rigging in Kotli’s LA-10 constituency. Rana Sanaullah, who is also the prime minister’s adviser on political affairs, alleged that PPP President in AJK Chaudhry Yasin was involved in election rigging and that presiding officers involved in the act had been apprehended. In an audio clip played on Geo News , he also demanded the AJK government and the AJK prime minister arrest a patwari he identified as Qaisar and interrogate him on the matter to locate others involved in the alleged rigging. Sanaullah said the election results in the constituency would not be acceptable to his party until the completion of this “inquiry”. While there was no official statement from the AJK government explicitly referring to the incident, a statement released by the Press Information Department late on Sunday said two presiding officers in Kotli had been arrested after it was reported that instead of reaching the relevant polling stations they had gone to “a residence”. “When the incident was reported, the returning officer issued directives to confiscate the polling material provided to the two presiding officers and replace them. “The returning officer took the polling material into his custody, removed the presiding officers from their duties and had them arrested,” the statement said. It added that action was being taken against them according to the law while two new presiding officers had been deployed in their place at the relevant polling stations. For his part, PPP’s Nadeem Afzal Chan responded to Sanaullah’s allegation in a video statement, saying that his party had been pointing out from “day one that you have been announcing projects [in AJK] and your federal ministers are present at government offices on the day of polling”. “So our first demand is that the federal government’s machinery should not interfere [in the elections] at all,” he said, further referring to the PML-N’s provision of e-buses to Mirpur and Muzaffarabad over the past few days. He also alleged the use of government resources in elections, demanding an end to it. Chan stressed the need for fair and transparent elections, saying: “We will not let rigging happen at any cost. Have some patience and let people cast their vote.” In a separate post, the PPP urged the Election Commission to take notice of the PML-N’s alleged “attempts to influence polling” in Union Council Throchi of the LA-12 constituency (Kotli-V), where Yasin is the PPP candidate. PPP AJK Election Cell Incharge Sardar Abdul Shakoor said that PML-N candidate Raja Riasat Khan allegedly entered “polling stations along with armed men and is trying to influence the polling process” in the constituency where the PPP AJK president is contesting. Shakoor further said that “slow mobile phone service” was creating difficulties in communication for residents, the media and rescue authorities. The PPP urged the Election Commission to ensure security at polling stations and an “independent, just and peaceful electoral environment”. The PPP also accused the PML-N of “interfering in the polling process” in the LA-8 constituency of Kotli. The party alleged in a post on X that the PML-N was trying to interfere in and disrupt the polling process at the Raj Mahal polling station. The PPP demanded that the Election Commission take notice of the matter, ensure fair, transparent and peaceful polling, and take action against those violating the election code of conduct. Bilawal vs Nawaz The PPP and PML-N, which are allies in the Centre, have been engaging in a war of words lately and taking jibes at each other, as the two parties emerge as major contenders in the AJK race. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari and ex-premier Nawaz Sharif were both participating in canvassing in the lead-up to the polls, with observers seeing this election as a contest between the two. Addressing a public rally in AJK’s Mirpur on Friday as part of his party’s election campaign, Nawaz had named Bilawal and said Kashmir should not be mistaken for Kashmore, nor Mirpur for Mirpurkhas — districts of Sindh where the PPP has been in power for years. The PML-N had also given 10 e-buses to Muzaffarabad and Mirpur as a “gift” and announced development schemes, prompting the PPP to decry poll code violations. Bilawal on Sunday responded to Nawaz’s jibe, saying that whether it’s Kashmir or Kashmore, Mirpur or Mirpurkhas, their residents were “not ready to bargain away their rights”. He also directly commented on Nawaz and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s announcement of “gifting” electric buses and hospitals on wheels to people of AJK before the election. “Something built with the public’s money is not a gift from any politician — it is the public’s right,” he said, adding that he wanted to secure for the people of Kashmir the right to governance, the right to ownership, and the right to employment. CEC urges citizens to vote, warns against disrupting polls On Sunday, AJK Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal urged more than 1.4 million registered voters to turn out in large numbers to elect their representatives. In a video message, the CEC said elaborate security arrangements had been made for the polls, with security forces and Quick Response Force teams deployed at polling stations and security also being ensured for voters travelling to and from polling stations. He warned that anyone attempting to disrupt the polling process would face strict legal action. Voting under way at a polling station in Kot Jamil, Mirpur, Azad Jammu and Kashmir on July 27, in the first phase of general elections in AJK. — Photo provided by author The warning followed the announcement by the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) on social media about a planned long march from Mirpur division towards Muzaffarabad on Sunday. A core member of the JAAC, Umar Nazir Kashmiri, had claimed that caravans would converge at the Rawalakot sit-in, before marching towards Muzaffarabad after Zuhr prayers on the election day. However, when Mirpur police deputy inspector general (DIG) was asked about the protest call given by the banned outfit, the official told Dawn on Sunday evening that not a single person had turned up anywhere to participate in any Rawalakot-bound rally. Meanwhile, AJK Chief Secretary Khushal Khan also warned of strict legal action against anyone attempting to disrupt the polling process or disturb public order afterwards.

The Pakistan Stock Exchange’s (PSX) benchmark index opened the week on a strong note, gaining more than 6,000 points during intraday trade. The KSE-100 index had gained 4,501.33 points to reach 175,522.53 points by 9:50am from the previous close of 171,021.20 points. By 10:30am, the index had gained 5,068.88 points to reach 176,090.08 points. By 2:13pm, the index had gained 6289.50 points to reach 177,310.70 points. Awais Ashraf, director of research at AKD Securities, said investor sentiment improved after the US and Iran paused military strikes, raising hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Middle East conflict and the resumption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. “The easing of geopolitical tensions has also increased the likelihood that the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) will maintain the policy rate in today’s monetary policy announcement,” he said. “We expect the SBP to adopt a cautious stance and keep the policy rate unchanged at today’s Monetary Policy Committee meeting, as it is likely to assess further developments in the Middle East and the economic impact of the recent flood situation,” he said. Nevertheless, the ongoing “disinflationary trend, a comfortable external account position, weakening leading economic indicators, and a contraction in money supply continue to support the case for monetary easing in the coming months”, he said. Meanwhile, Mettis Global , a web-based financial portal, attributed the rally to “easing geopolitical tensions and a sharp decline in global oil prices”, saying it improved investor sentiment. Iran and the US held their fire on Monday, handing Gulf shipping and the oil industry a respite from missile strikes as Donald Trump’s UN envoy said the president was “giving talks some space”. Oil prices also tumbled on Monday as investors breathed cautious sighs of relief at the pause in combat. The price of a barrel of international benchmark North Sea Brent crude shed more than seven per cent at one point early on Monday to briefly drop back below $90, while US counterpart West Texas Intermediate was down four per cent at $85.45 a barrel. The stock market had remained under pressure last week as the benchmark KSE-100 index lost 2.7 per cent amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, rising international oil prices and cautious investor sentiment. Water supply to parts of Karachi resumes after power at Dhabeji pumping station restored. KARACHI: Water supply to several parts of Karachi resumed in phases on Monday after electricity supply was resumed at the Dhabeji pumping station, around 22 hours after a power breakdown, Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation spokesperson Abdul Qadir Shaikh told Dawn . The spokesperson said K-Electric (KE) had restored power supply to the pumping station at 7:20am on Monday, around 22 hours after a cable fault suspended the supply at 8:43am on Sunday. He said the “prolonged outage had resulted in a shortfall of nearly 48 million gallons of water in the city” and the affected areas included parts of North Nazimabad, Nazimabad, Gulberg Town, New Karachi, Landhi, Korangi and Scheme 33. “Following the restoration of electricity, water supply to the affected areas has resumed in phases,” the spokesperson said. The Dhabeji pumping station, Karachi’s primary water intake point, is highly dependent on uninterrupted electricity. Even brief outages result in immediate service disruptions. The power breakdown on Sunday had resulted in the temporary shutdown of three pumps at Dhabeji, which KWSC initially attributed to a cable fault. The water utility’s spokesperson had told Dawn that a technical team had reached the site to rectify the fault. However, a KE spokesperson had clarified that the fault in KDA Pumping Feeder 2, which supplies electricity to the Dhabeji Pumping Station, “is internal in nature and is not related to K-Electric”. “Power supply to 19 out of 22 pumping motors at the Dhabeji Pumping Station is continuing as normal,” the spokesperson had said, adding that a power utility team was in contact with the relevant authorities to assist KWSC in addressing the fault. On Monday, after the power was restored, the KWSC official said while speaking to Dawn that the electricity supply had been disconnected due to a cable fault, and whether the fault in KE’s cable was internal or external, it was the power utility’s responsibility to rectify it. Dawn reached out to KE for further details, but there was no immediate response. Earlier this month, an electricity outage at Dhabeji had affected its K-2 Pump House, where the manifold chamber and main valves developed a fault. As a result, three major pumps at the K-2 Pumping Station had been temporarily shut down and water supply to several areas of Karachi was affected. Last month, on June 1, supply from Hub Pumping Station was also suspended to parts of Karachi due to a fault in KE’s main cable. KWSC said that the power suspension had resulted in a daily water shortfall of 85 million gallons per day (MGD) for the city. It was the third consecutive day of power failures at key pumping stations disrupting distribution across the metropolis. On May 31, the city faced a shortfall of 122 MGD after electricity supply to the North East Karachi Pumping Station was disrupted due to a fault in K-Electric’s main cable. The outage came just a day after an emergency shutdown at the Dhabeji Pumping Station, caused by a fault in a transformer at the grid station, forced 10 of the station’s 21 pumping units to shut down.

India's Cockroach Janta Party demands release of protesters after reports of detention. India’s youth-led “cockroach” movement, whose protests have forced the education minister’s resignation, urged authorities on Monday to release all demonstrators detained in weeks of rallies nationwide . The online Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which organised protests over exam paper leaks and other irregularities, said they had received reports of students held in detention, particularly in the states of Assam, West Bengal and Bihar. “Any failure to release those detained or withdraw criminal cases would amount to a breach of public trust,” the protest group said in a statement, adding they would take “further necessary steps” if their demand was not met. The statement comes two days after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister over repeated failures in the conduct of competitive exams that have fuelled anger among millions of young Indians. The CJP accused the government of backtracking after authorities had assured them that no punitive action would be taken against protesters. The movement has won millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May by 30-year-old public relations graduate Abhijeet Dipke. It emerged initially as a satirical response to Chief Justice Surya Kant reportedly likening young people to “cockroaches” and “parasites” during a court hearing. The movement has since broadened its agenda to include concerns over unemployment, opportunities for young people and what it describes as Modi’s increasingly authoritarian style of governance. Tens of thousands of protesters, mainly students, rallied last week in New Delhi and other cities, demanding Pradhan’s resignation and broader reforms of the examination system. Demonstrations in the Indian capital turned violent on July 20 when a crowd attempted to march towards parliament from the Jantar Mantar protest site. Police fired tear gas and used batons to disperse the protest, triggering clashes and a wave of detentions. The protests have emerged as one of the biggest challenges to Modi since his re-election for a third term in office in 2024. The issue reverberated in parliament on Monday, with repeated disruptions as opposition lawmakers demanded a response from the government over last week’s police crackdown . Despite the disruptions, the government introduced legislation in the lower house seeking tougher penalties for examination paper leaks. A series of exam irregularities have undermined trust in India’s testing system, including the leak of a medical entrance question paper that forced more than two million candidates to retake the test. Another dispute involving the online marking of examinations taken by nearly two million high school students has further fuelled public anger.

Leo Austria opens up on health scare. San Miguel Beer head coach Leo Austria opened up about undergoing an angioplasty procedure during the PBA break, explaining that side effects of his medications have kept him away from the team through its first three games. Austria said a routine check-up revealed blockages on his arteries which required him to undergo the procedure. “We had a medical check-up para maka-comply kami sa renewal ng GAB license. And then, the result, we found out there’s something wrong with my ECG. After a week, nakita namin ‘yung result, and then immediately, pinakita ko sa mga cardiologists, Dr. Tony Leachon and Rommel Galvez,” recalled Austria. “He said sa akin, you have to undergo a stress test kasi makikita kung anong klaseng puso meron ka. Ini-scan, and then there was something wrong. To confirm everything, kailangan mag-undergo ako ng angiogram and then na-confirm na my arteries [are] blocked,” he added. The diagnosis actually came as a shock for Austria, who revealed he is experiencing no symptoms and was even active during the team’s practice sessions and participating in some pickup basketball games. “I’m so lucky because the doctor told me na, 'You are a walking (time) bomb.' Buti hindi ako nag-collapse. My friend Tony Leachon, he has a team sa Manila Doctors, inarrange niya lahat, and then all of a sudden, nagkaroon ako ng angioplasty,” explained the veteran mentor. Austria made his first public appearance since the procedure in San Miguel’s 110-96 loss to NLEX, although he stayed behind the bench with assistant coach Peter Martin calling the shots for the fourth-straight game. Austria, however, assured that he’s already well and good, although he has been dealing with discomfort due to the side effects of his medications. “The problem is yung side effect ng medication nagkakaroon ng rebolusyon sa tiyan ko. Bloated ang tiyan ko very uncomfortable, the worst thing is nangyayari yung bloating in the evening,” explained Austria “Except yung kulang sa tulog and I can’t focus on my game plan or practice plan. Regarding sa my heart wala nang problema,” he added. The 68-year-old mentor said he is confident he can be back to work any time soon. “I’m confident na I can go back. It’s just a matter of time, kailangan makabalik ako 100 percent,” said Austria.

Charlie Fleming reacts to James Graham's coming out. Charlie Fleming has spoken publicly for the first time about former co-star James Graham's recent decision to come out as a trans woman, saying she fully supports her friend's journey toward living authentically. During the cast launch of Regal Entertainment's "Haunted Carnival," an official entry to the 2026 Metro Manila Film Festival, Charlie admitted she was caught off guard with James' announcement. She related, "I was actually really surprised because it wasn't something that I expected." Charlie and James worked together on GMA dramas "Royal Blood" and "Widow's War," where they developed a close friendship. Despite her initial surprise, Charlie said she has nothing but admiration for James. "But I'm really just supportive of her, whatever decision she makes. I'm really proud that she moved to the U.S. to study and that she's becoming the person she wants to become." She added, "And I'm just so proud that she has the courage to share that even to the world. You know how the world is cruel. The world is full of judgment, but she was able to show that side of herself and she wasn't scared of it." Charlie said they no longer keep in regular contact but remain on good terms. "No, we do not communicate now, but we do have our circle of friends who still communicate with her from time to time. We still follow each other and like each other's posts, so we're okay."

Tough draw for Alex Eala at DC Open. Alex Eala braces for another tough test to kick off her North American hard-court swing after being drawn in the bottom half of the bracket at the Mubadala DC Open in Washington DC, United States this week. The world No. 29 Eala is competing unseeded in the WTA 500 event and is scheduled to face Chinese wildcard Zheng Qinwen in the opening round. Though a wildcard entry, the 23-year-old Zheng packs an experience that includes ranking as high as No. 4 and making into the finals of the 2024 Australian Open, and winning the 2024 Paris Olympics gold medal. She also beat then 18-year-old Eala in their lone meeting at the semifinals of the 2022 Hangzhou Games before eventually winning the gold. An elbow surgery, however, sidelined her in the second half of last year and is slowly making a return this year. Apart from Zheng, other prominent athletes that Eala could face deeper in the tournament world No. 2 Elina Svitolina, seventh seed Canadian of Filipino descent Leylah Fernandez, four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka, 2020 Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin and eighth seed Emma Navarro. The DC Open is just the first of Eala’s tournaments leading to the US Open slated late next month.

600 cops deployed to secure SONA in NIR. BACOLOD CITY – The Police Regional Office-Negros Island Region (PRO-NIR) has mobilized nearly 600 personnel in the region to ensure the peaceful, orderly, and secure conduct of the fifth State-of-the-Nation Address (SONA) of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Monday, July 27. All units in the region have been placed on alert, and personnel remain vigilant, disciplined, and mission-focused as they relentlessly prevent any threat to peace and order. Police Brig. Gen. Romano Cardiño, PRO-NIR director, emphasized that the safety and security of the public remain their foremost priority throughout the national event. “We respect and uphold every citizen’s constitutional right to freedom of speech and peaceful assembly, and we remain committed to protecting those rights,” Cardiño said in a statement. He called on people to exercise these freedoms responsibly and within the bounds of the law. Cardiño said that these personnel which is on top of the PRO-NIR’s regular deployment aims to sustain police operational readiness, intensify monitoring efforts, and ensure the immediate response to any security concern that may arise in connection with the event. They are also in close coordination with partner agencies, force multipliers, and local government units to guarantee a unified and effective security effort before, during, and after the event.

Security for Marcos at ‘maximum’ after explosives found near DOJ, Senate — Palace. Malacañang said security for President Marcos should remain at the "maximum level" following an explosion near the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the discovery of a suspected improvised explosive device (IED) near the Senate hours before the President delivered his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA). Speaking to reporters at the Batasang Pambansa before the SONA on Monday, July 27, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the President's security should not depend on whether security threats had been reported. "Kahit may pagsabog o wala, dapat ang proteksyon sa Pangulo ay to the maximum level, alam naman natin 'yan (Whether there is an explosion or not, the President's protection should always be at the maximum level, we all know that)," she said. Asked whether security should be tightened further following the incidents, Castro said she would leave operational decisions to the Philippine National Police (PNP) but stressed that authorities should strengthen security measures. "Hindi ko masasabi sa PNP, pero definitely dapat (I cannot speak for the PNP, but definitely it should be)," she said. The Palace Press Officer said she had not yet discussed the incidents with President Marcos before the SONA, but added that the police should intensify security efforts. "Sa ngayon, hindi kami nakapag-usap ng Pangulo (As of now, we have not spoken with the President),” Castro said. “Pero, definitely, iyong mga kapulisan natin dapat mas matindi ang pag-iingat at ang seguridad (But definitely, our police should exercise greater vigilance and strengthen security)," she added. Earlier Monday, the DOJ confirmed that an explosion believed to have been caused by an IED occurred near the entrance of its Padre Faura headquarters shortly after midnight, although no injuries were reported and authorities said the compound remained secure as the investigation continued. Authorities also recovered a suspected improvised explosive device near the Senate along Diokno Boulevard in Pasay City on Monday morning, prompting an investigation and heightened security, although Senate proceedings continued as scheduled.

David Jonsson to play T'Challa's son in 'Black Panther 3'. Marvel Studios is keeping the momentum going as it introduced the newest actor set to don the Black Panther mantle. Academy Award-winning director Ryan Coogler announced during Marvel Studios’ Hall H presentation at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, that British actor David Jonsson has been tapped to play the new Black Panther in a film set to hit theaters on December 15, 2028. David received a loud ovation as he joined co-stars Letitia Wright, Winston Duke, and Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige onstage. “Thank you to this amazing family that I have the honor and privilege and the blessing to join,” David said from the stage as the audience screamed and cheered, with some sections breaking out in Wakanda chants. He will don the mantle of the Black Panther for the film. The actor is a recent Hollywood breakout, with key roles in "Alien: Romulus" and "The Long Walk". He was also part of the main cast for the first two seasons of "Industry." The "Black Panther" film franchise kicked off with the 2018 title, starring Chadwick Boseman as T’Challa. Chadwick passed away in August 2020 at the age of 43 following a private four-year battle with colon cancer. "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever" revealed that T’Challa had a young son with Nakia (Lupita Nyong'O). Since this is Marvel, the sequel could use a time jump or other story elements to make him older. The movie will also follow next year’s "Avengers: Secret Wars" and could have a major impact on the wider MCU. During the unveiling, Ryan shared that the film will focus on the young prince's journey. "The last time we got to make a movie, we introduced a character who is the son of the character that the great Chadwick Boseman played, our T'Challa, in that film. And today, I want to tell you that in this next film, he grows up and he comes of age," Ryan said. In an interview with Entertainment Weekly, Letitia Wright, who plays the role of Shuri, mentioned how excited she is to welcome David to such a big role. "The news was really beautiful to hear because I have a personal connection to David. To see the full circle of that today, I’m still living in it. We’re both still checking in with each other about it," she said. One of the highlights of this year’s Marvel panel at SDCC was the unveiling of Ryan Gosling as Ghost Rider in an upcoming film directed by Shawn Levy, who is also directing next year’s "Star Wars: Starfighter."

UST savors sweeping golden finish. It was short but sweet for the University of Santo Tomas Golden Tigresses. Marching into their first tournament following the departure of key senior players and in the absence of their injured main setter, the Golden Tigresses found a way to bring out their fierce growl and translate it into a breakthrough championship in the 2026 Shakey’s Collegiate National Invitationals. UST came out firing on all cylinders and captured the throne in a sweeping fashion to punctuate the Espana-based squad’s dominance in the international-flavored weeklong tournament backed by Shakey’s Pizza Parlor, Peri-Peri Charcoal Chicken, Potato Corner, and R and B Milk Tea. The Tigresses rolled past every obstacle for an impressive perfect seven-game romp capped by a come-from-behind, 22-25, 25-8, 25-12, 25-22, winner-take-all championship win over College of Saint Benilde on Sunday, July 26, at the Playtime FilOil Arena in San Juan. “Siyempre, sobrang happy dahil ‘yun nga nakuha namin ‘yung championship,” said UST head coach Shaq Delos Santos, whose squad dropped only a total of two sets the whole competition. “Sabi ko nga medyo short ‘yung preparation namin but ang good thing kasi ‘yung response din ng mga players and also coaches sa sistema na ina-adjust namin. I think ‘yun ‘yung malaking bagay. Good thing dito, nakita rin namin kung ano pa ‘yung mga kailangan naming i-improve. Sobrang dami pa namin kailangan ayusin,” added the architect of the Tigresses’ last UAAP championship 16 years ago. Skipper Regina Jurado and Most Valuable Player Angge Poyos stepped up not only on offense but also in their roles as leaders of a Tigresses side filled with young guns. The duo delivered the much-needed points in the title showdown with Jurado pumping in 21 points and Poyos scoring 20 as UST surpassed its third-place finish in 2023 by capturing the elusive crown in the competition supported by Jetour, Baic, Eurotel, Victory Liner Rent & Go, F2 Logistics, Summit Natural Drinking Water, PusoP.com and Smart Sports. Rookie Kim Rubin, who helped UST’s high school team rule the Shakey’s Girls Volleyball Invitational League Rising Stars Cup and was named MVP last May, added 12 points while middle blocker Blessing Unekwe scored seven of her 10 points on kill blocks, highlighting the Tigresses’ collective team effort. “Hindi naman naging sobrang hirap for us na i-guide sila kasi sumusunod din naman sila and kung ano yung system na meron sina coach talagang sinusunod lang namin. And ayun nga nakuha namin ang championship,” said Poyos, who took over as one of UST’s leaders after the graduation of former team captain and top libero Detdet Pepito. Setter Arlene Waje, meanwhile, embraced the playmaking position after Cassie Carballo was forced to sit out the National Invitationals due to a leg injury. Waje effectively filled the big shoes left by Carballo by dishing out 22 excellent sets in the finale to help the Tigresses pour 56 kills. “Sarap pala mag-champion. Nakalimutan ko na eh. Ganun pala ‘yung pakiramdam na nagtsa-champion. Sobrang thank you kay Lord kasi ‘yung opportunity na makuha namin yung championship this tournament even though short time lang ng tournament na to, sobrang laki para sa amin,” Delos Santos said. Having tasted the sweetness of winning a championship, UST is looking forward to completing a season title sweep when it marches back into action for the prestigious Shakey’s Super League (SSL) Preseason Unity Cup in September. The Tigresses eye redemption after a runner-up finish last year behind four-time champion National University. “Laking tulong nito, laking impact. And mas magiging inspired kami para trabahuhin pa namin 'yung mga susunod na tournament,” Delos Santos. All games in the competition, backed by technical partners Philippine Sports Commission, Commission on Higher Education, Mikasa, Asics, Rigour Technology and Team Rebel Sports, are available live and on-demand via PusoP.com livestream and Solar Sports.

Suspect in deadly Berlin Pride attack killed in confrontation with police. BERLIN (AP) — The suspect in the deadly Berlin Pride attack that left one person dead and 29 injured was shot and killed by police during a confrontation on Sunday in a suburb of the city, authorities said. Abdul Ballout, a German citizen with Lebanese roots, was killed following a search that lasted nearly 24 hours after the attack in downtown Berlin. Prosecutors said he had previously sought to join the militant Islamic State group. Ballout was suspected of driving a van into a crowd near Berlin’s Pride festival Saturday night before apparently stabbing others with a machete in what authorities believe was an Islamic extremist terror attack. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the attack occurred a few hundred meters (yards) from a party near the Brandenburg Gate that was supposed to close out the city's Pride festival. Ballout was tracked down around 6 p.m. Sunday at a garden in Spandau, a Berlin suburb, the city's police department wrote on X. They said he apparently ran toward officers with a sharp instrument, and police fired at least one shot. He died at the scene. Ballout was born in Germany, the minister said. His mother was naturalized in 2002, three years before he was born. Ashley Jump, a 26-year-old U.K. resident, had traveled to Berlin for Saturday’s Pride parade but had left the celebrations before the attack. They returned Sunday to leave flowers at a memorial near the crime scene in support of the LGBTQ+ community. “They’ll never erase us, we’ll never be gone,” they said. “As long as humanity has existed, we’ve existed. And as long as humanity exists, we will exist. We will not be removed.” Suspect convicted of ties to Islamic extremism Ballout traveled to Lebanon in 2025 with the goal of going to Syria to join the Islamic State group, Berlin prosecutors said Sunday. There, he made contact with several people who were presumed members of the militant group — or at least he believed them to be, prosecutors said. He was arrested in Lebanon last year and sentenced by a military court to three months’ imprisonment for offenses including incitement to religious and sectarian conflict. He returned to Germany after completing his sentence, where he was arrested at the Berlin airport. In May, a juvenile court in Berlin convicted Ballout of preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state, as well as publishing Islamic State propaganda on his Instagram account and other charges, prosecutors said. The court handed down a suspended sentence of 1 year and 10 months in youth custody, which Berlin prosecutors had appealed. The court said it took Ballout’s months of pre-trial detention in Germany and Lebanon into account. It also said it considered that Ballout had confessed to the crimes, appeared to distance himself from the militant group and no actual threat had ever materialized. He was released from detention pending the appeal. Berlin's Pride festival one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ celebrations According to police, a white van drove into the Tiergarten park around 10 p.m. and hit several people before colliding with a tree. The closing party at the Pride festival, known as Christopher Street Day, was ongoing at the time next to the Brandenburg Gate, a short distance away. The party followed a parade with some 80 trucks that had made its way through downtown Berlin earlier in the day. The attack did not occur at the festival, along its route or at the closing party. Rather, the violence took place a few hundred meters (yards) away on a track in the Tiergarten park. The van drove into a crowd that was likely a mix of festivalgoers and other locals or visitors. Police said a woman was killed. On Sunday afternoon, hundreds of mourners gathered at a memorial at the iconic gate. They hugged each other and laid down flowers, candles, rainbow flags and homemade signs, including a cardboard one that said: “the only thing more powerful than hate is love.” Hundreds of thousands had come to Berlin to celebrate on Saturday, though it’s unclear how many were still at the festival by late evening. It’s one of Europe’s largest LGBTQ+ celebrations. “We are simply stunned by what happened,” said Andre Lehmann, a top official with the main national LGBTQ+ association, LSVD+. “This suspected attack hits the heart of the queer community.” Amsterdam says it will celebrate freedom in the wake of Berlin attack Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged the nation to remain united in the aftermath of the attack. “I would like to say this to Christopher Street Day participants here in Berlin but also across Germany: Don’t let yourselves, let us not let ourselves, be intimidated," he said. "These acts have only one purpose: They aim to divide our society. They want to take away from us the most important thing we have: Namely our openness and our freedom.” Dobrindt said he expected security measures at other major events in Germany, including Pride events elsewhere, to be reviewed and, if necessary, significantly boosted. Berlin has seen Islamic extremist attacks before. In December, 2016, a rejected asylum seeker from Tunisia plowed a hijacked truck into a Christmas market, killing 13 people and injuring dozens. He was killed days later in a shootout in Italy. In February last year, a Spanish tourist was stabbed and seriously wounded at Berlin’s Holocaust Memorial, an attack that saw a Syrian man convicted in March and sentenced to 13 years. This week, Amsterdam will be hosting World Pride alongside its own annual Pride celebrations. Mayor Femke Halsema said authorities and organizers “are closely monitoring the security situation” after the Berlin attack but aim to prevent any extra measures getting in the way of celebrating freedom and love.

LeBron James picked Philly, eight years after billboards asked him to play for Sixers. LeBron James wound up picking Philadelphia, and no billboards were required. Back in February 2018, a businessman named Asher Raphael arranged for three billboards to be placed a few miles outside of Cleveland in a lighthearted effort to woo James to the Philadelphia 76ers. James decided later that year to leave the Cavaliers and join the Los Angeles Lakers. The billboard bit seemed futile. Instead, maybe it was just premature. James announced Friday, July 24, that he's joining the 76ers in what he said will be the “last decision” of his playing career — and, finally, Raphael can say the billboard investment from eight years ago paid off. “I was in the middle of a board meeting and my phone was going off like something was on fire," said Raphael, the co-CEO of Power Home Remodeling, a Pennsylvania-based firm with offices around the country. "And it was people from all walks of life, employees, former employees, friends from all over the country being like: ‘It worked. Process completed.’ It was the coolest thing.” The original billboard idea was loosely based on the award-winning 2017 film “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri,” and was simply intended to be something fun. It wound up going viral. Raphael ordered billboards with the messaging of “Philly Wants LeBron” and “Complete The Process” — a nod to the 76ers' infamous “process” of rebuilding, with hopes of becoming a contender. The third billboard showed where James would fit on the court with the other Sixers starters at the time: Dario Saric, Ben Simmons, Robert Covington and Joel Embiid. Of those, only Embiid remains with the 76ers. Raphael considered ordering more billboards this summer but didn't place any orders. Turns out, he didn't need to. “We just wanted to drop a seed that Philly wanted him," Raphael said. "I think a lot of people think of Philly as a great sports town, but opposing teams think of it as kind of an intimidating place. And we just wanted to drop a seed that he would be welcomed here and he’d love it.” Raphael's company got some name recognition from the billboard move in 2018, and he said it was a great morale boost to employees. And he fully believes James coming to Philadelphia, to play alongside Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe, is going to pay off for a city that hasn't seen its NBA team win a championship since 1983. “Philly, right now, is on fire," Raphael said. “At that moment, we became an undeniable contender. And if he comes to Philadelphia and we get that title and that trophy after 44 years, the country will see what Sixers fans are about.”

Search for 17 missing crew after Vietnamese cargo ship sinks in South China Sea. HANOI, Vietnam (AP) — A multinational search by Vietnamese, Philippine and Chinese rescuers was underway on Sunday for 17 crew members missing after a cargo ship sank in bad weather off a Chinese-occupied shoal in the disputed South China Sea, The Vietnamese cargo vessel Khoi Nguyen 18, carrying 62 people, sank late Saturday near Fiery Cross Reef, which is a Chinese-built island and a military outpost in the hotly contested Spratly Islands. Of those on board, 45 crew members have been found and 17 others are still reported missing. The vessel “sank while operating in bad weather conditions in the East Sea,” Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Pham Thu Hang said. The Philippine Coast Guard said it deployed a patrol vessel and an aircraft to help search for the missing crew members after receiving a request from Vietnam. Chinese rescue ships and helicopters, along with other vessels in the area, joined the operation. Vietnamese authorities said fishing vessels had joined the search and that the families of those on board had been notified. Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said that it was coordinating with Vietnam’s coast guard “for other operational information needed to guide the search and rescue response.” She said the coast guard was also using a search planning system to improve the chances of locating the missing crew members and had issued a navigational warning urging ships transiting the area to keep watch and assist if it was safe to do so. The Philippine Coast Guard said the operation was being conducted under international maritime agreements and bilateral cooperation with Vietnam. Vietnam’s Foreign Ministry thanked China for its swift assistance and said it hoped the search would continue to find the remaining crew members. China has become increasingly aggressive in asserting its claims in virtually the entire South China Sea, through which about $5 trillion in global trade transits each year. The sea passage is also believed to be sitting atop vast undersea deposits of oil and gas. As well as China and the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan also have overlapping claims in the strategic waterway. A Planet Skysat captured this image of Fiery Cross Reef in the South China Sea on May 3, 2020. Constructed between 2014 and 2017, Fiery Cross Reef is one of China’s seven artificial islands in the Spratly Islands and represents a continued military presence in the region. (Wikipedia)

Liza Soberano says DreamWorks' 'Forgotten Island' helped heal fears after leaving PH: 'I was scared'. Liza Soberano has opened up about the uncertainty she faced after leaving the Philippines to pursue a career in the United States, revealing that she feared the move would cost her both her career and the people closest to her. The actress said those emotions were still fresh when she auditioned for DreamWorks Animation's "Forgotten Island," making the project especially meaningful. "It's actually quite serendipitous how this whole project came together for me," Liza said. "I just moved back to America from the Philippines when I got asked to audition for this role, and a big part of me moving was so that I could find growth as an artist and just as a human being." Leaving, she admitted, wasn't as exciting as it looked from the outside. Liza recalled worrying that the backlash she received over her decision to seek opportunities abroad would follow her for years. "I actually received a lot of kind of backlash from that," she said. "I was scared of leaving the Philippines because of that backlash. I was scared that I won't have a career to come back to, or friends and family that would still care about me after being away for so long." Working on "Forgotten Island" gradually changed that perspective. The film's story, she said, reminded her that the people who truly matter remain part of your life, even when distance separates you. "Through this film, I realized that even when you are going away from home or leaving a few people behind, you have all these memories and you have this deep connection and relationship that you can always come back to," she said. Liza also found something familiar in her character, Raissa. As the eldest of 10 siblings, she said she's used to keeping everyone together, much like the character she voices. "I'm the eldest daughter so I feel like in 'Forgotten Island,' Raissa's kind of that. She's always wrangling the whole gang just trying to get them to follow the plan or stick to the plan. And I am very much like that, too. If things don't go the way I imagine it, I'm gonna have a meltdown."

Gas prices push motorcycle sales near 1 million mark in first half. The country’s motorcycle sales grew by 3.6 percent to nearly 940,000 in the first half of the year as demand remained strong despite higher fuel prices, the Motorcycle Development Program Participants Association Inc. (MDPPA) said. Data from the MDPPA showed that industry sales reached 939,528 units from January to June, up from 907,054 units sold in the same period last year. Automatic motorcycles accounted for the largest share of the market, with 655,004 units sold or 70 percent of total sales. Business motorcycles, which primarily support delivery services, ranked second with sales reaching 148,989 units. Meanwhile, mopeds or underbone motorcycles registered 107,632 units sold, equivalent to 11 percent of overall sales. Also sold during the first six months were street motorcycles with 24,346 units, big bikes with 2,994 units, and other motorcycle categories, which combined for a total of 563 units. MDPPA said the growth this year was largely fueled by the industry’s first-quarter performance, with sales growing by 11 percent to 496,868 units from 447,865 units in the same period a year ago. In contrast, motorcycle sales dropped by more than four percent to 442,660 units from April to June, down from 462,007 units in the same period last year, based on MDPPA data. “The gains achieved in the opening quarter helped keep overall first half sales firmly in positive territory,” MDPPA said. Despite a softer second quarter, MDPPA President Erwin Estrada said the local industry maintained its positive momentum, given the continued importance of motorcycles as a practical and cost-efficient mode of transportation. Demand for motorcycles has remained relatively strong in recent months as Filipinos seek fuel efficiency amid higher pump prices resulting from hostilities in the Middle East. This has persisted despite elevated inflation, which has prompted increases in the prices of goods and services. “The industry's continued growth demonstrates that consumers recognize the value motorcycles provide through affordability, fuel efficiency, and dependable transportation for work, business, and daily life,” said Estrada. MDPPA expects the industry’s growth trajectory to continue through the rest of the year, supported by sustained demand for motorcycles. MDPPA is the country’s leading motorcycle industry group, counting motorcycle giants Honda, Kawasaki, Suzuki, and Yamaha as its members. Based on data from the Federation of Asian Motorcycle Industries (FAMI), sourced from the MDPPA, the group’s motorcycle output increased by six percent to 631,630 units from January to May, compared with 596,234 units in the same period last year. FAMI data showed that Indonesia remained the largest motorcycle market within the regional group, with sales reaching 3.13 million units. Vietnam ranked second with 1.37 million units sold, while the Philippines placed third.

‘Hindi kawalan’: Palace unfazed by SONA boycott, says President is 'what matters'. Malacañang has shrugged off the decision of several senators to skip President Marcos' fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA) on Monday, July 27, saying their absence would not affect the administration. Speaking to reporters at the Batasang Pambansa before the President's annual address, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the President was the one who mattered during the event. "Hindi naman sila kawalan (They are not a loss),” she said. “Ang Pangulo po ang importante dito at yung mga opisyal na interesadong makinig sa Pangulo (What is important here is the President and the officials who are interested in listening to him)," she added. Castro said officials who were unwilling to listen to the President should not be compelled to attend "So yung mga ibang opisyal na wala namang balak makinig sa Pangulo ay hindi natin pipilitin (Those officials who have no intention of listening to the President will not be forced),” she said. "Kung mas gusto nilang mas magbakasyon, mag-ibang bansa, hindi natin sila mapipilit (If they would rather go on vacation or travel abroad, we cannot force them)," she added. Her remarks came after several senators publicly announced they would skip this year's SONA, including Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano, who said he would instead watch the speech on television as a form of protest and deliver a "kontra-SONA" the following day. Senators Pia Cayetano, Imee Marcos and Robin Padilla also confirmed they would not attend, while Imee Marcos said Sen. Loren Legarda would likewise be absent. Vice President Sara Duterte would also be absent as she remained abroad, marking the fourth consecutive year she has skipped President Marcos' annual SONA.

POC paves resolution of volleyball leadership crisis. The Philippine Olympic Committee (POC) moved closer to resolving the country’s volleyball leadership crisis after all board members of the suspended Philippine National Volleyball Federation (PNVF) agreed to resign. “That’s the first step, and they all agreed to resign,” said POC President Abraham “Bambol” Tolentino after the volleyball general assembly on Monday, July 27, in Parañaque City. The assembly also approved key constitutional amendments, including the creation of a 13-member board with athlete representatives, seats for the UAAP and NCAA, a POC representative, and the removal of the chairman's position. The secretary-general will now be appointed by the federation president. “This is to promote inclusivity and ensure stakeholders prioritize the national teams,” Tolentino said. With the amendments approved, the POC will convene another general assembly on Aug. 10 to discuss the roadmap toward fresh elections for the federation. The POC has been overseeing the PNVF following its suspension by the FIVB, a move that followed sanctions imposed by the Philippine Sports Commission and the POC.

1,000 Bicol cops on standby for SONA. LEGAZPI CITY – The Police Regional Office-5 (PRO-5) has readied 1,000 personnel from its CARE (Crowd Management Advanced Reactionary Force Engagement) contingent as standby support for security operations during President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s fifth State-of-the-Nation Address (SONA) Monday, July 27. In a statement, PRO-5 spokesperson Police Lt. Col. Malu Calubaquib said the personnel are prepared for immediate deployment to Metro Manila, particularly in Quezon City, where the SONA will be held, should additional support from regional police units be needed to ensure the smooth and safe implementation of security measures. “We are prepared to deploy the 1,000 police personnel. We are just waiting for instructions from our central office if additional support is needed,” she said. Calubaquib said other CARE personnel remain on heightened alert to maintain peace and order throughout the Bicol region. “They are assigned to provide security and immediate response to any incident related to the expected gatherings and activities in the Bicol region,” she added. She noted that the contingents are part of the Bicol Shield Initiative, which aims to strengthen the police force's preparedness, capabilities, and rapid response for major events, not only within the region but also in neighboring areas that may need reinforcement. “Through coordinated operations and continuous readiness of the police force, PRO-5 remains committed to ensuring security, order, and public safety at all times,” Calubaquib said. PRO-5 assured Bicolanos that comprehensive security measures are in place to ensure the peaceful conduct of the President's SONA while maintaining uninterrupted police services and public safety throughout the region. The public was urged to remain vigilant, cooperate with law enforcement authorities, and immediately report any suspicious persons, activities, or incidents to the nearest police station or through the police emergency hotlines. (PNA)

Gatchalian says Senate to continue pushing for economic reforms: 'The task is urgent, clear'. Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said on Monday, July 27 that the passage of bills promoting economic reforms will remain on the topmost priority of the Upper Chamber this Second Regular Session of Congress. Gatchalian made the declaration during the opening of the Senate’s plenary session, as he highlighted the need for the country’s economy to regain its footing. “The most urgent point of concern, therefore, is getting the Philippine economy back on track. To that end, this Congress will prioritize legislation aimed at reinvigorating the nation’s economy in support of this administration’s objectives,” Gatchalian said in his opening speech. “Furthermore, genuine economic recovery cannot be measured by growth figures alone. It must be felt in the things that really matter—affordable goods and services, secure jobs and food on the table,” he said. Among the priority measures of the Senate will include the proposed 2027 national budget, the Senate leader reaffirmed. “The national budget is our most powerful tool for stimulating the economy. It is imperative that the 2027 national budget be passed on time,” he said. He also said the livestreaming of the Bicameral Conference Committee and the uploading of all budget documents to the Senate Transparency Portal will continue this budget season. “These reforms must continue so our people can see that the government is accountable and reliable,” he said. Aside from the prompt and thorough passage of the national budget for next year, Gatchalian said the Senate will focus on dealing with five major issues, namely: high commodity prices, low take-home pay for workers, high electricity bills, lack of infrastructure and transportation, and job insecurity. “Regardless of our status in life, we all feel the weight of these problems,” he said. Also included in the list of measures the Senate will prioritize is the amendments to the Rice Tariffication law, the Ginhawa Bll, which seeks to increase the take-home pay of workers, the bill strengthening the mandate of the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC), amendments to the Downstream Oil Industry Deregulation Act, the Masterplan for Infrastructure and National Development (MIND) bill, and Magna Carta for MSMEs. “Let us build an economy worthy of the strength of our people, one where work provides security, daily needs are within reach, and the fruits of growth are felt in every Filipino home,” the Senate chief said. “The task before us is urgent and clear. Let us come together as one Senate, one government, one people, and set our nation towards a horizon of progress for every Filipino, in every generation,” he reiterated.

Aiden Lazaro becomes first-ever homegrown baseball talent to train at IMG Academy. Aiden Lazaro made a giant stride in his young and promising career after becoming the first-ever Filipino homegrown recruit at IMG Academy, one of the world's premier sports training centers located in Bradenton, Florida. Lazaro, a 13-year-old shortstop and catcher, could become the first homegrown Filipino to play in Major League Baseball (MLB) if he makes it through the tough process of further harnessing his skill and someday be drafted. “I'm excited to immerse myself in a new training environment and learn from everyone at IMG Academy who helped develop some of the top athletes and professional players. I look forward to bringing home everything I gain from this so I could contribute more to my teams in the Philippines," said the Ateneo Grade 8 student Lazaro. "I'm very thankful to IMG Academy for welcoming me into its baseball and holistic athletic training program and for working closely with my mom over the past few months to help create exciting opportunities for my future. I'm humbled by this privilege and I'm ready to work hard to make the most of it,” he added. Lazaro, who entered the sport at age of five, excelled immediately in baseball, having been part of Ateneo’s juniors baseball crew when he was Grade 7 student. He also a gold medalist with the National Capital Region (NCR) in last year’s Palarong Pambansa in Laoag, Ilocos Norte – a great follow-up to his feat of Most RBI (runs batted in) Award at the Asian Baseball Championship in Japan where captained the country's U12 National Team in 2024.

Cops arrest 51 people for vandalism, other offenses ahead of SONA. At least 51 people were arrested for various violations that include vandalism ahead of the State of the Nation Address of President Marcos, the Philippine National Police (PNP) said on Monday, July 27. Aside from vandalism, PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr. said those arrested violated the Batas Pambansa 880, or the Public Assembly Act, and local ordinance relating to covering face when entering public or private establishments or when stopped on public roads and crime prone areas. “We have a reason to have a valid arrest and they were accosted because of violations of ordinances and special laws and local ordinances especially those covering their faces,” said Nartatez. “You remember what happened in September last year? We will not allow them to create trouble on the roads that affect the peaceful conduct of protest actions,” he added. Nartatez was referring to the incident in Manila last year when a group of teenagers wearing masks and bonnets attacked policemen and started setting up fire on police barricades. Scores of policemen were injured during the surprise attack that happened at the height of the anti-corruption rally at the Luneta in Manila on Sept. 21 last year. He confirmed that 51 people were arrested and they were caught in the act of violating the law, adding that most of them were collared for vandalism. He said appropriate criminal charges will be filed against them. More than 21,000 policemen were deployed in various parts of Quezon City and Metro Manila as part of the security measures for Marco’s 5th SONA.

Katy Perry slams White House after using her song 'Firework' in military strike video. Katy Perry is speaking out after the White House's official TikTok account used her song “Firework” in a video showing footage of military strikes. The video, posted last Thursday, featured lyrics from her Grammy-nominated album "Teenage Dream", including the words "boom, boom, boom," played over clips of bombs exploding. Its caption read: "Iran has been warned." Expressing her frustration, Katy posted on X (formerly known as Twitter), saying, "I am deeply appalled and angry to see ‘Firework’ used on the @WhiteHouse TikTok account as a backing track for video footage of military strikes. I did not approve this, I was not asked, and I absolutely do not condone it." “I wrote this song to be an anthem of hope, healing, and inner strength for people going through their darkest personal moments,” she continued. "To see a message of self-worth and upliftment weaponized to soundtrack destruction and violence is a complete violation of everything my song stands for." Katy concluded her statement: "My music is for bringing people together, not celebrating warfare." Earlier this year, Kesha condemned the White House for using her song "Blow" on TikTok featuring fighter jets in the sky with the caption, "Lethality."

'Matinong tao yan': Sandro Marcos believes Gatchalian can get Senate up and working. House Majority Leader Ilocos Norte 1st district Rep. Sandro Marcos expressed confidence that Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian would be able to turn the upper chamber into a well-oiled machine this second regular session. "It's good that the Senate has now organized everything. And I'm sure under the leadership of SP Gachalian, the legislative mill will continue or will go back to functioning as efficiently as possible," Rep. Marcos told House reporters on Monday, July 27. "Kailala mo naman si SP, matinong tao yan (You know SP, he’s a decent person). And I'm sure [he] will get the Senate up and working as quickly as possible. Monday marked the start of the second regular session of the ongoing 20th Congress. It fell on the same day as President Marcos' fifth and penultimate State of the Nation Address (SONA). The presidential son gave these remarks as part of his reflection on the legislative output of the bicameral Congress, with the passage of the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council (LEDAC) priority measures serving as the yardstick . Congress is composed of the 318-strong House of Representatives and the 24-member Senate. ""With regards to the role of the House, 26 of the 52 [LEDAC measures] were passed in the first regular session. We plan to--we're actually ahead of schedule," Rep. Marcos said. "So we will hope to continue the momentum that we started in the first regular session on to the second regular session. And I am sure that over the coming months and by the end of this legislative calendar, we will continue to pass the LEDAC priorities of the administration," he said. For a bill to prosper into a law, it must gain final approval from both legislative chambers. Of the 52 identified priority measures of the Marcos administration, only one--the reset of the first parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM)--has been enacted. Asked if such low number of enacted LEDAC bills could be attributed to the recent disarray in the Senate, Rep. Marcos gave an affirmative answer. "You know, that's definitely, I would have to say that that's definitely a factor. You know, the more, how do I say this? The more political gulo (chaos) that there is, the less time there is to work. I mean, everyone knows that, di ba (right)?" Before Gatchalian, the Senate Presidency was passed from Senator Vicente "Tito" Sotto III to Senator Alan Peter Cayetano during a controversial coup d'etat on May 11, 2026.
