Gatchalian was formally elected Senate President on June 17, 2026, during a special session of Congress, wherein he succeeded Cayetano after a leadership dispute.

Motorists brace for fuel price surge on SONA week. Motorists are expected to rush to gasoline stations on Monday, July 27, to beat another round of steep fuel price increases taking effect on Tuesday, July 28, with the anticipated queues likely adding to traffic on the day of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA). Effective Tuesday, select oil companies such as Unioil Philippines, Jetti Petroleum, and Petro Gazz are set to raise diesel prices by ₱7.30 per liter and gasoline prices by ₱6.80 per liter. The Department of Energy (DOE) has yet to confirm the prescribed price adjustments for the week, while current inventory levels remain undisclosed as of this writing. Last week, gasoline (RON95) averaged ₱71.80 per liter, diesel averaged ₱88.40 per liter, and kerosene averaged ₱117 per liter. Energy Secretary Sharon Garin earlier said the DOE is preparing for any new presidential orders by the time of Marcos ’ penultimate SONA. The DOE chief emphasized that the country’s oil situation will likely be highlighted in this year ’s SONA , as the government and state-run sovereign wealth fund (SWF) manager Maharlika Investment Corp. (MIC) work on increasing the nation’s fuel inventory to shield it from global oil market volatility. The DOE is also awaiting action from the Senate on amendments to the Oil Industry Deregulation Law, which would give the agency the power to prescribe price adjustments and other measures during energy emergencies and direct government-wide assistance to secure a stable fuel and energy supply, among others. Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said the Senate plans to prioritize the proposed amendments as soon as possible.

Battle for stronger signal as Converge, TNT collide. It’s a battle of which team has the stronger signal to boost their respective campaigns as corporate and industry rivals Converge and TNT lock horns in Group A action of the PBA Season 50 Governors’ Cup at the Ninoy Aquino Stadium on Tuesday, July 28. Tip-off of the clash is at 7:30 p.m. with the FiberXers aiming to get back on the winning track and the Tropang 5G desperate to find their groove after a roller-coaster start to their title-retention bid. Setting the table to the duel is the collision between Group B surprise leaders Phoenix and Blackwater in the first offering at 5:15 p.m. Converge actually had a great start to the conference, winning its first three games before dropping a 122-128 loss to San Miguel. As good as its 3-1 record so far, the weakest link for the FiberXers is import Jalen Hudson, who only averaged 12.25 points, 6.75 rebounds and 3.25 assists. With that, the FiberXers have decided to bring back former import Jamal Franklin for their game against the Tropang 5G. In his last stint in the PBA, Franklin averaged 34.0 points, 11.7 rebounds, and 7.6 assists to steer Converge to a 6-5 record in the same conference two seasons ago. The frontline of Justin Arana and Justine Baltazar are expected to once again lead the way alongside Juan Gomez de Liano, Alec Stockton and Mikey Williams. TNT, on the other hand, is dealing with more than just its import woes but also the absence of the team’s key players. Import Darius Days has been playing subpar for the Tropang 5G who are missing players like Calvin Oftana, Jayson Castro, Brandon Ganuelas-Rosser and Kelly Williams. After opening the conference with a close 106-103 win over Macau, TNT has suffered back-to-back losses to Titan Ultra, 103-87, and then Terrafirma, 101-96. Of course, the defending champions are hoping to avoid falling into a third straight defeat but it will need more from days as well as local stars Jordan Heading, Rey Nambatac and RR Pogoy.

Sandiganbayan orders arrest of Uswag Ilonggo solon Jojo Ang over alleged graft. The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered the arrest of Uswag Ilonggo Party-list Rep. James “Jojo” Ang Jr. and issued a Hold Departure Order (HDO) after finding probable cause to try him for alleged graft. “After a careful review of the resolution and its supporting documents, as well as the records, the court finds that probable cause exists in this case, pursuant to Section 5, Rule 112 of the Revised Rules of Criminal Procedure,” the anti-graft court stated. “Accordingly, let a warrant of arrest be ISSUED against accused James Ang Dit Ang, Jr. Let a Hold Departure Order (HDO) be ISSUED against the accused.” The Third Division is chaired by Associate Justice Karl B. Miranda. On July 25, the Office of the Ombudsman (OMB) announced that it had filed 14 counts of graft against Ang before the Sandiganbayan for allegedly retaining an interest in a construction firm that obtained ₱214 million in Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) contracts while he was serving in Congress. Assistant Ombudsman Jose Dominic “Mico” Clavano IV said Ang retained an interest in a construction firm that secured ₱214 million in DPWH contracts and received nearly ₱199 million in payments while serving in Congress. The OMB noted that the Constitution bars members of Congress from holding any financial interest in government contracts while serving their terms. On July 18, the Ombudsman announced that the complaints against Ang and other congressmen have moved to the preliminary investigation stage.

Filinvest Land’s Kaya Sulit initiative lowers barriers to lot ownership. A profound shift in consumer behavior is reshaping the Philippine real estate landscape: modern Filipino families are increasingly bypassing hyper-congested metropolitan cores to secure prime, regional land as a primary wealth-building asset. Responding directly to this demand for inflation-hedged, suburban stability, Filinvest Land has launched its "Kaya Sulit" home deals, offering immediate savings of up to 35 percent on select residential lots in partnership with leading financial institutions. By lowering the barrier to entry, this nationwide initiative gives buyers the financial runway to lock in highly appreciating land today and build on their own terms tomorrow, seamlessly fueling local economies while anchoring multi-generational security. According to recent data from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the median price of a home in the National Capital Region (NCR) has reached an astronomical 8.36 million pesos, while residential properties in Areas Outside the National Capital Region (AONCR) remain far more accessible at a median of 3.39 million pesos. Backed by a historic 35.63 billion dollars in cash remittances sent home by overseas Filipinos, buyers are acting on this price gap. As part of a diversified property portfolio, acquiring a residential lot serves as an exceptional standalone investment for long-term capital appreciation and wealth preservation. This behavioral shift allows families to hedge their wealth against inflation while maintaining the financial liquidity and creative freedom to design and construct their dream homes entirely at their own pace. "We recognize that the ultimate aspiration for every Filipino family is to establish a secure foundation that they can truly call their own, on their own terms," says Aven Valderrama, Filinvest Land senior vice president and Residential Business head. "Owning land is a powerful tool that builds generational wealth and stimulates local business activity right where people reside. Through these attainable deals, we are lowering the barrier to entry, giving everyday families the confidence to spark their own personal growth and lay down roots in thriving, well-connected communities that expand alongside their aspirations." By prioritizing these regional residential spaces, Filinvest Land does not merely develop real estate; it actively creates the physical infrastructure that underpins localized economic prosperity. Each lot acquired within these master-planned developments serves as a localized cell of economic activity. As families settle in these hubs, they naturally attract retail establishments, academic anchors, and critical infrastructure, establishing a highly productive cycle where localized commerce thrives. This intentional regional footprint, backed by a comprehensive track record serving over 160,000 families across the archipelago, ensures that real estate transactions directly stimulate provincial business ecosystems, keeping economic productivity close to home. Flexible, high–value purchase schemes designed for every buyer The Kaya-Sulit program introduces highly customizable terms designed to optimize upfront capital, making lot ownership exceptionally accessible. Under this limited-time initiative, aspiring homeowners can secure a premium lot for as low as a ₱ 7,000 reservation fee, with light monthly downpayments starting at just ₱ 7,000 and comfortable monthly amortizations of ₱ 11,000 on select participating projects. For those who prefer to stretch their full payments over a period of two years, Filinvest Land provides a baseline of up to a 30 percent discount under flexible terms. Meanwhile, investors seeking immediate ownership can maximize their capital with up to a 35 percent discount on the Total List Price (TLP) for cash payments settled on the spot or within a 7- to 30-day window. Demonstrating the nationwide scale and high-value accessibility of this campaign, Filinvest Land has rolled out the program options across prime expansion corridors. Investors looking to anchor their wealth can access premier horizontal communities, including Fairway View in Cavite, Amarilyo Crest Residences and New Fields in Rizal, Montebello and South Peak in Laguna, and Blue Isle in Sto. Tomas, Batangas. Down south in the rapidly progressing economic centers of the region, Ocean Cove answers the high demand for premium seaside land-banking. Secure your legacy: Take your first step To take advantage of the Kaya Sulit home deals and secure a premier residential lot, interested buyers can begin by exploring Filinvest Land's portfolio of participating lot-only developments on the official Kaya Sulit page. Through this dedicated portal, future property owners can easily compare regional locations, discover the community that best aligns with their lifestyle and financial goals, and connect with a dedicated Filinvest property consultant to customize their payment terms. By aligning value-driven property access with the practical economic realities of modern Filipino families, Filinvest Land transforms the dream of secure land ownership into an immediate, wealth-generating reality—seamlessly blending daily life with local livelihood opportunities to build a stronger, more resilient nation from the ground up.

Philippine banks hit record ₱208 billion profit as loan margins defy bad debt surge. Philippine banks generated record earnings in the first half of the year as robust lending margins cushioned the sector against rising credit loss provisions and persistent market volatility. Data from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) showed that net income across the banking system rose 5.2 percent year-on-year to ₱208.4 billion in the six months through June from ₱198.1 billion in the same period last year. This first-semester performance was buoyed by strong interest income, which offset continued losses in other areas. Banks’ net interest income climbed 13.1 percent to ₱638.9 billion as of June, up from ₱565 billion in the first half of 2025. This income represents the difference between interest earned and interest expenses, including provisions for losses on accrued interest from financial assets. Non-interest income saw a modest increase of 2.1 percent, reaching ₱122.2 billion compared to ₱119.7 billion last year. This category includes fees and commissions, trading income, and foreign exchange (forex) gains or losses. Notably, the industry still reported forex losses of ₱5 billion as of June, but this was a significant improvement from the ₱37.7 billion forex loss recorded in the same period in 2025. During the first half, the banking system’s total operating income rose 11.2 percent to ₱761.1 billion, compared with ₱684.7 billion a year ago. During the same period, non-interest expenses increased by a tenth to ₱422.1 billion from ₱384 billion in 2025. These expenses cover compensation and benefits, taxes and licenses, fees and commissions, and impairment losses. Notably, the banking sector’s total losses on financial assets reached ₱101.7 billion, a 38.2 percent increase from ₱73.6 billion in 2025. Provisions for credit losses also surged 32.2 percent to ₱111.3 billion from ₱84.2 billion last year. Further, bad debts written off reached ₱4.4 billion as of June, a 61.2 percent jump from ₱2.7 billion a year earlier. Writing off bad debts—such as non-performing or “soured” loans—allows banks to clean up their balance sheets by removing uncollectible accounts. Conversely, recoveries on charged-off assets rose 5.5 percent to ₱14.1 billion, up from ₱13.3 billion in 2025. As of end-June, the banking system’s total assets increased 2.3 percent to ₱31.13 trillion from ₱30.44 trillion in the previous month. Year-on-year, it rose by more than a tenth from ₱28.21 trillion in June 2025. Bank assets are mainly composed of deposits, loans, and investments, including cash, amounts due from other banks, interbank loans receivable (IBL), and reverse repurchase (RRP) arrangements, net of allowances for credit losses. During the period, the Philippine banking system’s total loan book expanded by 1.7 percent to ₱17.78 trillion from ₱17.48 trillion in May. Compared with last year, the total loan portfolio grew by nearly 12 percent from ₱15.88 trillion.

Cyberpunk is having a moment in 2026. A genre born from the anxieties of technology in the 1980s has gone nova. In a span of months apart, four foundational cyberpunk titles are going to appear on screen. Studio Trigger and Netflix confirmed the second season of the highly popular Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, is set to arrive later this year, with a new story and a new cast of characters. Fun little fact, while Edgerunners is based off of Cyberpunk 2077, the videogame itself is also based off of the tabletop boardgame by Mike Pondsmith simply called Cyberpunk, first released in 1988, and then updated in 1990 as Cyberpunk 2020. Meanwhile, Ghost in the Shell returns on screen as a more faithful adaptation to the OG manga. The new Science SARU series, which began streaming in July, is the first adaptation to work directly from Masamune Shirow's original 1989 manga rather than reinterpreting it, which is chaotic, raunchier, and lighter in tone but no less insightful instead of the meditative approach of Mamoru Oshii's 1995 animated film. In live action screens, Amazon has revealed the trailer for Blade Runner 2099. The original Blade Runner, released in 1982, starring Harrison Ford, is a monumental hallmark in cinema, providing the grimy, dark aesthetic of high tech blended with societal rot, which many future cyberpunk stories found its inspiration from, such as animated films like Akira (1988) and the 1995 Ghost in the Shell. The last of this list also happens to be what started it all. Apple TV has announced Neuromancer, based on the novel by William Gibson, published in 1984. The story included what are now core cyberpunk traits, cyberspace and the matrix, mega corporations, and “high tech, low life.” It is interesting to note that four different cyberpunk stories share the same imagery, chrome, neon, and corporate skylines. It’s worth asking why these adaptations remain relevant–besides being cool, of course. And listening to what they have to say. Cyberpunk as a genre The term cyberpunk was coined by author Bruce Bethke in 1983, which he used to describe high tech, low life, or rebellious youth. Since cyber refers to computers, internet, digital, and other high technology, and punk as the rebelling against those technologies. Mainly because technologies end up ruling over people, creating a societal divide between rich and poor with nothing in between. If you look at cyberpunk stories, the antagonists are almost often megacorporations who own people through technology. And these megacorporations are large and powerful enough as if they were cosmic horrors themselves. Cyberpunk stories are dystopian, disguised as a utopian world. There is existential dread, where the people living in them either accept or reject the norm, and almost feel as if they don’t have a choice in the matter. Corporations are so powerful they own the government, and so they dictate what the people want. Outside the cities, are barren wasteland, and often the reason for its destruction is often cited as climate change and ecological disasters. Cyberpunk worlds tend to share a few recurring features. Megacorporations have absorbed most of the functions once held by governments. Body modification and neural implants are common, blurring the line between human and machine. Cities are dense, vertical, and perpetually lit by advertising, while the outdoors, nature, and public space have mostly disappeared. Information itself is treated as a place you can enter, steal from, and get lost in. And almost always, the protagonists are not powerful people. They're hackers, mercenaries, and drifters operating in the margins of systems built by people much more powerful than they are. Other traits that cyberpunk stories share involve sex work. Blade Runner 2049, sequel to the first Blade Runner, and starring Ryan Gosling, depicts women appearing behind glassed windows as if they were products to be bought or rented. They have giant holographic commercials that promote an AI companion called Joi. Seriously, “Joi.” You know if you know. In the wasteland, there are statues of women in suggestive poses, ruined and forgotten, as if they were discarded byproducts or simply too old. In 1995’s Ghost in the Shell, Makoto often strips naked to activate her optical camouflage. Yes, I am aware she’s actually wearing a skin tight suit, but it does not change the fact that she looks naked with discerning details to provide everyone with enough “research” materials, and it doesn't change the symbolism that she does not own herself (if she quits Section 9, she must return the cybernetic pieces of herself, which includes her memories). All the sex work and sexually explicit are representations of extreme commodification of the body. It is saying you don’t own yourself. But cyberpunk is also about freedom of expression. Body modification, fluid genders, chaotic art, hackings. These little things are acts of rebellion themselves, reclaiming what was lost to them. Cyberpunk is a genre about existential crisis, AI, and technologies by mega corporations. Many of these stories take place in the far future, and it should really go without saying, none of the settings happened instantly. It happened gradually, starting with one new product after the next, with slight nudges to condition consumers into thinking a certain way, while crippling individuals, who, unfortunately, cannot keep up. Writers in the 1980s were watching real deregulation, the growth of multinational conglomerates, and the first waves of corporate consolidation in media and computing, and extrapolating. Four decades later, the extrapolation reads less like fantasy, less like science “fiction.” A handful of technology companies now sit astride global communications, commerce, and increasingly, the infrastructure of artificial intelligence itself with market capitalizations that dwarf the GDP of most countries and lobbying operations that shape the laws meant to constrain them. Cyberpunk's central provocation, corporations might simply out-govern governments, is part of why the genre still feels less like prophecy fulfilled and more like a live diagnosis. It's not a coincidence that four different studios are returning to this imagery at a moment when conversations about tech-platform power, data ownership, and the political reach of a handful of companies dominate the news cycle in ways that would have felt like plot points in 1984. The other constant in cyberpunk is verticality is the literal, architectural verticality, used as a metaphor that barely bothers to hide itself. The wealthy live above the smog line, in towers and orbital rings, insulated from the world they've built underneath them. Everyone else lives in the "sprawl," the flooded, overcrowded, rain-slicked streets where Blade Runner's replicant hunters and Gibson's console cowboys make their living. Ghost in the Shell's Section 9 operates in a Japan where cybernetic enhancement has created new tiers of citizenship: Those who can afford full-body prosthetics and those who can't. Edgerunners' entire premise is built on the gap between the "corpo" towers of Arasaka and the street-level chaos of Night City's edgerunners, mercenaries who take on body modification and lethal jobs precisely because the formal economy has no place for them. Cybernetic enhancement, life extension, and access to cyberspace are luxuries in cyberpunk, not equalizers. The poor get the same technology eventually, but in cheaper, more dangerous, more exploitative forms, or they get left permanently behind. That's the "low life" half of the formula doing its work: Not poverty despite the technology, but poverty produced and enforced by it. And often we are led to believe that technology is meant to be a solution to problems. Yes, it still is. But “whose” problems are something worth asking about. That tension is arguably more legible to audiences now than it's ever been. Automation reshaping labor markets, AI systems built and controlled by a small number of firms, and widening gaps between asset owners and everyone else are not background themes anymore, they're frontpage stories, they make headlines, and they have strong believers. Cyberpunk didn't invent economic anxiety about technology, but it built an entire visual and narrative language for it, and that language is proving durable enough that four different studios, working independently, all reached for it in the same short span. All of this sounds very familiar, eh? I bet you see it everyday. With big tech gaining prominence in recent years, from developing products and services that make it hard for people to live without from communications to storing identifications, information, digital infrastructure, navigation, and human experiences such as videos and photos, followed by the rise of AI and AI data centers that take up finite resources and creates certainties within the workplace--which, management will say, AI won't replace humans, but humans with AI knowledge will replace humans, and people need to evolve and keep up--are exactly the words that creates that divide, instead of being the solution that finds ways to improve society as a whole, it's easy to see the world is headed toward a cyberpunk world. Maybe that's our best case scenario. People have better chances, it seems. Notable mentions of cyberpunk and cyberpunk elements, Ready Player One where people are addicted to the metaverse and WALL-E where humans have lost the will to do anything and simply consume anything shown to them.

Batangas bizman saved by bulletproof vest. A bulletproof vest saved the life of a 56-year-old businessman who was shot and wounded in an ambush in Sitio Balete, Purok 1, Barangay San Isidro, Lipa City, Batangas, on Sunday morning, July 26. Police identified the victim as Teodolo. Investigation said Teodolo was driving his truck when two unidentified men on a black scooter appeared and shot him. The victim jumped off his truck which crashed into a tree. He fled towards his house and was taken to a hospital. The suspects took the victim’s sling bag containing his cellphone and wallet before fleeing to an unknown direction. He sustained bullet wounds in his left arm and abdomen and he survived due to the bulletproof vest he was wearing due to an alleged threat against his life allegedly his brother over a land dispute. Manhunt and follow-up operations are ongoing.

After big win over SMB, is NLEX now for real?. NLEX’s era under new head coach Jimmy Alapag is off to a dream start after the team passed its first real acid test against PBA heavyweight San Miguel. The Road Warriors jumped on the Beermen right from the get-go, stretching the lead to as many as 25 before holding off the comeback in the fourth quarter to give Alapag a perfect 4-0 start to his coaching career. But does the win over SMB make NLEX now a legitimate contender? The impressive campaign sure had put the league on notice but for Alapag, he has been saying that there’s still a lot to learn for his team and they just had a great experience playing against a championship team. “Really proud of our guys. I think anytime you play a team like San Miguel, with all of their championship experience, it's always a great test for a young team,” said Alapag. “I'm really happy with the spirit of our guys. I think games like tonight will only allow us to continue to grow as a team and as a family,” he added. The 4-0 start for NLEX already ties the all-time franchise best conference start. The last few times that Road Warriors achieved the feat was during the 2023 Governors’ Cup with head coachFrankie Lim and import Jonathan Simmons and the 2022 and 2017 Governors’ Cup under coach Yeng Guiao with imports KJ McDaniels and Aaron Fuller, respectively. But for Alapag, if there’s anything that the win against SMB showed NLEX, it is the team’s resilience and poise. “I thought we were very resilient, especially in the second half. (Don) Trollano is one of the best shooters in the league and he got going, but I thought our poise in the second half was great for the young team that we have,” noted Alapag. “We were able to get stops and score when we needed to, to get the win,” he added.

Rise Energy Pop enters the beverage scene with a burst of grape flavor. Purple took over SM City Manila as Rise Energy Pop introduced its newest beverage through "A Pop of Surp-Rise," a launch event designed to reflect the brand's youthful personality. Music, games, performances, and interactive booths welcomed members of the media, content creators, influencers, and guests for an afternoon centered on the brand's first product, Rise Energy Pop Grape. The new carbonated drink is aimed at younger consumers juggling school, work, side hustles, content creation, and busy social calendars. According to marketing head Apple de Belen, the brand was developed after observing Gen Z's preference for beverages that are both refreshing and suited to their fast-paced lifestyle. "We noticed that younger consumers, especially Gen Z, are always looking for something new and exciting," Apple said. "They want drinks that are delicious, refreshing, and bagay sa kanilang fast-paced lifestyle. That inspired us to create something that offers an enjoyable beverage experience." Leading the lineup is Rise Energy Pop Grape, a sparkling grape-flavored drink that the company says is intended for casual occasions, whether during study breaks, gaming sessions, hangouts, or spontaneous outings. Senior brand manager Joanna Araullo said the brand was designed to fit naturally into the everyday routines of today's consumers. "When we created Rise Energy Pop, we wanted to offer something more than just a drink. We wanted a brand that naturally fits today's lifestyle—fun, enjoyable, flavorful, and exciting," she said. Araullo added that grape was selected as the launch flavor because it reflects the brand's energetic and playful identity. "For our launch flavor, we chose Grape because it perfectly captures the fun, vibrant, and playful personality of the brand. It's youthful, exciting, and expressive—exactly the kind of experience we want Rise Energy Pop to deliver. Even its signature purple color reflects the bold and energetic spirit of Rise. We can't wait for everyone to experience Rise Energy Pop and discover why 'Sarap Mag-Rise!'" The event also introduced three brand pillars—Refreshi-Rise, Yummi-Rise, and Invigo-Rise—through themed activity booths. Guests posed for photos in a grape-inspired installation, sampled the new beverage, and participated in arcade-style games and a claw machine challenge. Rise Energy Pop also unveiled its first campaign video featuring brand ambassadors Rabin Angeles and Angela Muji, alongside the brand anthem built around the tagline "Sarap Mag-Rise!" Rise Energy Pop Grape is now available in supermarkets, groceries, convenience stores, and sari-sari stores nationwide.

Converge tops Philippine broadband in H1 of 2026. Converge ICT Solutions Inc. maintained its position as the country’s broadband provider to beat after delivering the fastest internet in the first half of 2026, according to internet analytics firm Ookla. Based on Ookla’s analysis, Converge registered the highest connectivity score in the country at 73.14 from January to June. The company outpaced Globe Telecom Inc., which registered a score of 72.56, and PLDT Home Fiber, which scored 70.54. The connectivity score measures the combined network performance of an internet service provider (ISP), including speed, latency, and the quality of experience in web browsing and video streaming. In terms of speed, Converge secured the top spot with a score of 61.86, followed by Globe at 60.84 and PLDT Home Fiber at 58.46. Converge’s download speed reached an industry-leading 143.04 megabits per second (Mbps) in the first half, while its upload speed also topped the category at 136.24 Mbps. According to Converge, it also posted the country’s best latency score at 14.44. Lower latency ensures faster network response times for consumers, it said. Meanwhile, Globe claimed the top spot in the video streaming category with a score of 78.04, edging out Converge’s 77.91. However, the company led by tech tycoon Dennis Anthony Uy recorded the highest web browsing score at 90.91, ahead of both Globe and PLDT Home Fiber. Converge said its performance in the first six months extended its dominance in Ookla’s assessment of the local broadband industry, particularly in internet speed, since 2022. “Being awarded the fastest provider for four straight years, best ISP for three years, and now confirmed to have the best latency, is a testament to our consistent efforts to deliver superior performance,” Converge Chief Operations Officer (COO) Benjamin Azada said in a statement on Monday, July 27. Converge intends to turn this achievement into a long-term competitive advantage by continuing to invest in network upgrades and expansion. “The company continues to invest heavily in network capacity and technology services to deliver meaningful internet solutions to households, businesses, and public institutions across the country,” it said. Earlier, Uy told reporters that the company remains committed to spending up to ₱23 billion in capital expenditures (capex), even as operating costs increase due to supply chain volatility. He said Converge remains on track to expand its reach in Visayas and Mindanao through the development of around 900,000 fiber ports within the year.

‘Kiyapo’ death toll remains at 3 as aid tops P10 million. Tropical Storm Kiyapo has left three people dead and one missing while government assistance to affected communities has exceeded P10 million, according to the latest National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) report released on Monday, July 27, hours before President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. delivers his State of the Nation Address (SONA). The NDRRMC said the storm has claimed one life in Davao and two in Sarangani due to drowning and fallen debris. One person also remains missing in Sarangani. The latest report showed that 63,606 families or 295,066 individuals have been affected by Kiyapo across eight regions. The affected regions were Ilocos (Region 1), Cagayan Valley (Region 2), Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), Western Visayas (Region 6), Zamboanga Peninsula (Region 9), Davao (Region 11), Soccsksargen (Region 12), and Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). Of those affected, a total of 1,760 families or 7,550 persons were staying in 31 evacuation centers. The storm also damaged 671 houses, including 246 that were destroyed and 425 that sustained partial damage. Government agencies have so far extended P10,093,344 worth of assistance to affected communities. The latest figures were released as President Marcos was set to outline his administration's priorities in his fourth SONA, where disaster resilience and climate adaptation are expected to remain among the government's key agenda following a series of weather disturbances that affected several parts of the country this year. Kiyapo developed over the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) last week and brought heavy rains and strong winds to parts of Mindanao. The storm enhanced the southwest monsoon in some areas, triggering floods and prompting evacuations in vulnerable communities. It left PAR on Saturday, July 25, leaving a trail of destruction. The NDRRMC said damage assessments and validation of casualties are continuing as local government units and national agencies sustain relief and recovery operations in affected areas.

Local shuttlers gun for strong start in historic BWF International Challenge. The Philippines is set to host a world-class badminton tournament for the first time as the Philippine International Challenge 2026 gets underway with the qualifying rounds Tuesday, July 28, at Gameville Central Park in Mandaluyong City. The International Challenge is a Grade 3, Level 1 tournament on the Badminton World Federation Continental Circuit, alongside the International Series and Future Series. The event awards ranking points that count toward the BWF World Rankings. "The association sent bids to host these tournaments, a proposal to the BWF through Badminton Asia, to host an International Challenge and an International Junior Series this year," said Philippine Badminton Association secretary-general Shawntel Nieto, as the country prepares to stage a BWF-sanctioned tournament for the first time. "Gratefully, they accepted, and with the support of and with the go-signal from boss MVP, we were able to plan out and bring it to life. So, we’re very excited about that." The tournament will run until August 2, with an International Junior Series tournament set to follow the following week at the same Mandaluyong venue. Leading the men's singles field is Kazakhstan's Dimitri Panarin, who returns to the Philippines after his main draw appearance in the 2022 Badminton Asia Championships. Joining him among the top five seeds are India's Manraj Singh and Alap Mishra, Indonesia's Christian Adinata, and Malaysia's Jing Hong Kok. On the women's side, 21-year-old Thai standout Tidaporn Kleebyeesun headlines the draw as the top seed. She is followed by fellow Thais Yataweemin Ketklieng and Pornpicha Choeikeewong, Indonesian-born Azerbaijani Keisha Fatimah Azzahra, and Malaysia's Siti Zulaikha. Fresh off their campaigns in the recently concluded Philippine National Badminton Open, Clarence Villaflor and four-time national women's singles champion Mika De Guzman, both ranked World No. 122, will lead the Philippine contingent as top-10 seeds in their respective draws. Reigning three-time national men's singles champion Jelo Albo also banners the local challenge in men's singles. Also advancing directly to the main draw are Philippine National Badminton Open men's doubles champions Julius Villabrille and Solomon Padiz Jr., women's doubles runners-up Lea Inlayo and Jeya Pinlac, and the tandem of Hailene Diaz and Naeomi Gulpany in the women's doubles Round of 32. Smash Pilipinas begins its campaign in the qualifying rounds with Mark Velasco and JR Pandi. Velasco takes on Saudi Arabia's Mehad Shaikh, while Pandi faces Australia's Ken Richardson. A victory by either player will send them to the main draw alongside Villaflor and Albo. In mixed doubles qualifying, newly crowned national champions Villabrille and Andrea Princess Hernandez will face Patricia Barredo and Filipino-born Australian Jan Mark Sotea for a main draw berth. Padiz Jr. and Mary Destiny Untalan will also look to qualify when they take on Vietnam's Le Minh Son and Mai Thi Thanh Ngan. Meanwhile, Lance Vargas and Carlo Remo will battle Laos' Namboun Luangamath and Phonesack Sookthavy in the men's doubles qualifying draw.

DILG: Over 42,000 barangays to receive P200K each for college scholarship, community development programs. Over 42,000 barangays nationwide will each receive P200,000 to fund their respective college scholarship and community support programs, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said on Monday, July 27. The DILG, through Memorandum Circular No. 2026-038, outlined the implementation of the program, under which each barangay nationwide will receive P200,000 from the Office of the President through the Socio-Civic Projects Funds (SCPF) project. “The program seeks to empower local government units (LGUs), reinforce effective barangay governance, and expand opportunities for young Filipinos to complete their education while enabling communities to respond to their immediate development priorities,’’ the DILG said. Of the P200,000 allocation, the DILG explained that P100,000 shall be dedicated to the Bagong Pilipinas Barangay Scholars Program, through which each barangay will select five incoming fourth-year college students for school year 2026–2027 to receive a P20,000 "Finisher Fund" to help cover essential academic expenses and complete their college education. According to the guidelines, beneficiaries must be bona fide residents of the concerned barangay and belong to vulnerable households that are at risk of dropping out of school. Preference shall be given to students whose families have no member who has completed tertiary education. Barangays may also prescribe additional eligibility criteria, provided these are properly documented and implemented in a just, fair, and transparent manner. Meanwhile, the remaining P100,000 shall be allocated for the “Assistance for the Barangay’’ component, which will support development priorities identified by barangays based on their immediate operational and community needs. Further the DILG noted that the eligible interventions include the procurement of public service equipment, administrative and office equipment, street lighting facilities and disaster risk reduction and management equipment, among others. Likewise, the DILG disclosed that the barangays may augment the allocation using their own local funds to complete identified development priorities. However, the guidelines provide that the assistance shall not be used for infrastructure projects, honoraria, salaries, wages, or other similar personnel-related expenditures.

ACEN nears 1-GW clean energy hub in Zambales. Ayala-led ACEN Corp. is transforming Zambales province into one of the country’s largest renewable energy (RE) hubs, with nearly one gigawatt (GW) of combined solar and battery energy storage projects either operating or under development. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Monday, July 27, ACEN said its Zambales portfolio will have about 948 megawatts (MW) of combined solar capacity. This includes the 585-MW SanMar solar project in San Marcelino town, being developed across more than 500 hectares (ha) of unutilized, lahar-covered land, and 363-MW Palauig solar project. At present, 450 MW of the total capacity is already operational, with the remainder under construction and scheduled for completion by 2027. To support dispatchability and maintain grid balance, ACEN has also started constructing 1,660 megawatt-hours (MWh) of battery energy storage systems (BESS) co-located with its solar assets in the province. These facilities will store excess energy generated during peak daytime output for release into the grid during periods of high evening demand. Once fully operational, the solar developments are expected to generate approximately 1,400 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of clean electricity annually—enough to supply around 340,000 households and offset nearly 800,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions each year. To transport the clean power to consumers, the listed energy firm has completed 14 kilometers (km) of transmission infrastructure connected to Luzon grid, with an additional 22 km currently under construction. Beyond power generation, the developments have spurred local economic activity in host communities. ACEN noted that approximately 80 percent of its project workforce was sourced locally, primarily from the Ayta indigenous peoples (IPs) community. The company has also built six km of roads and concrete bridges, opening access routes for remote indigenous communities to travel to town centers, schools, and health facilities. “At ACEN, we believe RE projects should create value far beyond the electricity they generate,” said Miguel de Jesus, ACEN managing director and chief operating officer (COO) for Philippine development and operations. “In Zambales, we are not only building one of the country’s largest RE hubs—we are investing in infrastructure, creating local jobs, supporting indigenous communities, and strengthening the country’s long-term energy security.” By relying on indigenous clean energy resources, ACEN said these projects are designed to reduce the country’s dependence on imported fossil fuels, mitigating exposure to global market price swings and foreign exchange (forex) fluctuations. - Gabriell Christel Galang

Police probe Malasiqui shooting; Mistaken identity eyed. MALASIQUI, Pangasinan – Police are looking at the possibility that the fatal shooting of 24-year-old Harryvel Belo here over the weekend may have been a case of mistaken identity. The victim's mother, Cherry, an Overseas Filipino Worker (OFW) from Malaysia, said this in an interview with the Manila Bulletin in their home in this town on Monday. Cherry, who returned home two days after the shooting Saturday, reiterated her appeal for justice and called on authorities to ensure that those responsible are held accountable. She said that Harryvel was looking forward to finally being reunited with her for good in the Philippines. "Napagusapan na namin na sa pagbabalik ko sa Pilipinas hindi na muna ako magtrabaho sa Malaysia, pero nabigo kami at hindi na matupad na kami magkakasama," Cherry said. (We discussed my return to the Philippines and stop working in Malaysia anymore. We failed and we won’t be united anymore) Cherry said her sacrifice and hard work in Malaysia were all meant to provide a better future for her family. Probe underway Police said they are working diligently to solve the incident as quickly as possible. A report submitted to Police Regional Office-1 Director Police Brig. Gen. Jovencio S. Badua Jr. said investigators have leads that may help identify and arrest the suspects. Police urged people with relevant information to cooperate with authorities and help solve the incident. The victim and two companions were standing on a roadside when two unidentified men on a motorcycle appeared and shot them. Bello and his 23-year-old male companion were declared dead in a hospital. Their female companion, 21, is recuperating in a hospital.

Marcos says duty is to Filipinos, not family, as anti-graft crackdown reaches cousin Romualdez. President Marcos declared that his loyalty is to the Filipino people—not to his family or political allies—as he highlighted the administration's anti-corruption campaign during his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA). In his speech, the President, who was visibly serious from the moment he started his address, acknowledged that the investigation into alleged irregularities in flood control projects has already reached his cousin, former House Speaker Martin Romualdez. The President disclosed that, according to the Ombudsman, multiple cases against a former House Speaker are now nearing filing. "Masakit man sa akin ito, pero kailangan nating gawin ang tama (Painful as this may be for me, we have to do what is right),” he said. “Hindi ako pangulo ng aking pamilya. Hindi ako pangulo ng aking kaibigan. Ako ay Pangulo ng Pilipinas at ang tungkulin ko ay sa inyo, ang aking mga kapwa Pilipino (I am not the president of my family. I am not the president of my friends. I am the President of the Philippines, and my duty is to you, my fellow Filipinos),” he added. President Marcos recalled that it had been a year since he first exposed corruption in flood control projects and said the administration fulfilled its promise to pursue those responsible. "Gaya ng aking ipinangako sa inyo, nagsagawa tayo ng malawakan at mala-limang imbestigasyon, na walang pagkiling kahit kanino man (As I promised you, we conducted a broad and exhaustive investigation without favoring anyone),” he said. “Masusi nating sinuri at sinundan kung saan tayo itinuro ng ebidensya. Lahat ng kailangang gawin ay ginawa natin upang matunton ang puno't dulo (We carefully examined everything and followed where the evidence led us. We did everything necessary to get to the bottom of it),” he added. Reporting on the government's year-long investigation into the alleged corruption, Marcos said contractors, senior Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials, and lawmakers have already been charged and jailed. He said the government conducted what he described as a broad and exhaustive investigation that followed the evidence without favor to anyone. Marcos added that authorities ensured that public funds intended for allegedly defective, fake, or non-existent projects would no longer be released to contractors and officials involved in the scheme. According to the President, nearly P25 billion worth of money and assets linked to the accused have been recovered, frozen, or preserved, with more than P800 million already returned to the National Treasury. He added that all assets eventually recovered from those found liable would be returned to the government's coffers, while the prosecution of the cases has been left to the Ombudsman and the strengthened National Prosecution Service. Marcos also expressed confidence that the courts would fairly resolve the cases, saying the "wheels of justice are moving." Beyond filing criminal cases, the President said the administration has begun institutional reforms within the DPWH, including hiring new graduates and career personnel, reviewing all infrastructure projects from planning to implementation, aligning construction material prices with prevailing market rates, and strengthening project monitoring through the Transparency Portal, Integrity Chain, and civil society participation. Marcos likewise credited public complaints submitted through the "Isumbong sa Pangulo" platform for helping uncover alleged anomalies, saying citizen participation remains essential in the fight against corruption. “Nakatulong ang lahat ng mga ulat at hinaing ninyo sa Isumbong sa Pangulo. Ang inyong pagbabantay at pakikialam sa pamahalaan ay ang susi sa paglaban sa katiwalian (Your reports and complaints through Isumbong sa Pangulo have helped. Your vigilance and participation in government are key to fighting corruption),” he said.

Special handbag makes Congresswoman Matibag's SONA outfit simple, dignified, and meaningful. This year's State of the Nation Address (SONA) by President Marcos was billed as "simple but dignified"--something that was extended to lady guests at the event as a reminder for their outfit decisions. Heeding the call for austerity was Laguna 1st district Rep. Ann Matibag, who instead chose to make her SONA outfit of the day more meaningful through her accessory of choice. Matibag brought with her on Monday, July 27 at the House of Representatives a stunning handbag made of pearls, which was apparently crafted by persons deprived of liberty (PDLs). This move from the lady solon reflected her "commitment to rehabilitation and second chances". According to Matibag, the bag represents her belief that every individual has the capacity to change when given the right opportunities, support, and dignity. As chairperson of the House Committee on Women and Gender Equality and president of the Zonta Club of Laguna, Matibag has consistently championed programs that promote livelihood, skills development, and rehabilitation for marginalized sectors. Among these initiatives is her support for products made by PDLs, whom she helps equip with sustainable skills and opportunities as they prepare to reintegrate into society. Matibag says supporting PDL-made products goes beyond recognizing craftsmanship--it is also an affirmation of every person's ability to rebuild their lives and begin anew. By choosing to carry the handcrafted bag on the opening day of the second regular session, Matibag demonstrated her belief that meaningful public service is one that creates hope, restores dignity, and opens doors to opportunities for all. The ranking lawmaker was accompanied by her husband, National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag to the SONA held at the House of Representatives in Batasan, Quezon City.

PBBM defends government's response to Middle East crisis, says PH acted swiftly to cushion impact. President Marcos has defended his administration's handling of the economic fallout from the conflict in the Middle East, saying the government responded quickly to protect Filipinos and mitigate the crisis' effects. In his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA) on Monday, July 27, the President said he could confidently face the people and tell them that the government acted accordingly and promptly to the still ongoing crisis. "Mga kababayan, sa ating pagbalik-tanaw, kaya ko kayong harapin at sabihin na ginawa natin ang lahat ng nararapat upang malunasan ang mga epekto ng krisis (My fellow Filipinos, as we look back, I can face you and say that we did everything necessary to address the effects of the crisis),” he said. “Agarang kumilos ang buong pamahalaan upang tumulong sa mamamayan. Sa katunayan, tayo pa ay hinangaan dahil sa bilis, liksi, at pagiging aktibo ng ating pagtugon (The entire government acted immediately to help our people. In fact, we were even admired for the speed, agility, and decisiveness of our response),” he added. Marcos said the government immediately declared a State of National Energy Emergency after the country felt the effects of the war in the Middle East and launched the Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) to protect vulnerable Filipinos. "Iisa ang ating misyon: UPLIFT — ang iahon ang ating nahihirapang mamamayan (We have one mission: UPLIFT—to lift up our struggling countrymen),” he said. The President said all government agencies were ordered to tighten spending and prioritize programs that directly addressed the crisis, while additional funding was channeled to frontline services and local governments to accelerate assistance. He added that nearly P58 billion in additional funds was released to local government units to expand assistance, adding that public funds recovered from corrupt officials were redirected to programs benefiting the people instead of being lost to corruption. OFWs Marcos said the administration first focused on assisting overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) caught in the conflict, noting that more than 2.5 million Filipinos work across the Middle East. He said more than 12,000 Filipinos had been safely repatriated since the war began, while more than 140,000 OFWs received food, financial assistance, medical aid, temporary shelter, and other forms of government support. According to the President, returning OFWs were assisted through the AKSYON Fund, the OWWA-Kabuhayan Program, Public Employment Service Office (PESO) referrals, and Bayanihan para sa Balikbayang Manggagawa job fairs, while others were helped secure overseas employment again. He also announced that returning OFW teachers would be deployed to public schools, saying, "Dahil dito sa Pilipinas, sila ang mga Ma'am at Sir (Here in the Philippines, they are our Ma'am and Sir).” Marcos added that the government continues to coordinate with foreign governments to ensure the safety of OFWs, especially after some Filipinos were reported dead or missing because of the conflict. Energy The Chief Executive said the administration leveraged its diplomatic relations to secure enough fuel supplies despite disruptions caused by the temporary closure of the Strait of Hormuz. He said the Philippines was able to source oil from Japan, South Korea, Oman, India, Russia, and China, ensuring enough fuel supply to last for nearly two months. He added that the government also coordinated with Iran to ensure the safety of thousands of Filipino seafarers passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Marcos said oil companies cooperated with the government by implementing staggered fuel price increases instead of sudden adjustments to ease the burden on consumers. He added that the government also required oil companies to implement successive price rollbacks whenever global conditions allowed. Food security President Marcos said the administration also acted to stabilize food prices by limiting increases in imported rice prices and cracking down on those who took advantage of the state of energy emergency. "Lahat ng posibleng gawin para mapababa ang presyo at mapabagal ang pagtaas nito, ginawa natin (We did everything possible to bring prices down and slow their increase),” he said. The President said job fairs were conducted nationwide as workers lost jobs during the crisis, including nearly 100 Labor Day job fairs offering almost 300,000 vacancies, where more than 6,000 applicants were hired on the spot. He added that wages for more than 100,000 beneficiaries under the Department of Labor and Employment's (DOLE) Integrated Livelihood and Emergency Employment Program (DOLE) and Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers (TUPAD) programs were also distributed during the nationwide job fair. Marcos said banks and electronic wallet providers were encouraged to reduce or waive online transaction fees, while financial institutions, including GSIS, SSS, NHMFC, and Pag-IBIG Fund, granted payment moratoriums to ease the burden on borrowers. He added that more than 26,000 metric tons of rice had already been distributed to more than 2.5 million families, with the program set to expand to eight million households. The President also cited the continued implementation of the Benteng Bigas Meron Na program, which he said has benefited more than 12 million Filipinos, alongside more than 800 KADIWA outlets that continue to connect consumers directly with farmers and fisherfolk. He added that nearly 2 million farmers and fisherfolk received assistance under the Presidential Assistance to Farmers, Fisherfolk, and Families (PAFFF) during the period of elevated fuel prices. Utilities and business relief The President said improved internet connectivity enabled more Filipinos to shift to online work and classes as fuel prices remained elevated. He acknowledged that electricity prices also increased because of higher oil prices and a stronger US dollar but said the government ordered refunds for consumers who were overcharged by electric utilities. Marcos said selected consumers were also allowed to pay electricity bills in installments from May to July, while utility companies were temporarily prohibited from disconnecting power service as long as payments were being made. He added that the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) is implementing a one-time tax abatement program this year to help microentrepreneurs whose businesses suffered because of the crisis. Transport Calling transportation the sector hardest hit by the crisis, President Marcos said drivers, operators, commuters, workers, and businesses all suffered from soaring fuel prices but stressed that the government could not allow public transportation to grind to a halt because it serves as "the piston of our economy." He said jeepney and UV Express drivers received cash assistance under the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) program, along with a P10-per-liter diesel subsidy, while more than 1.8 million transport workers also received financial assistance. For commuters, Marcos said the government expanded the Libreng Sakay program with the participation of several government agencies, while the Department of Agriculture (DA) also helped transport agricultural products to major trading centers. The President said the government also revived the Service Contracting Program for buses and jeepneys, allowing qualified operators and drivers to earn additional income based on the number of kilometers they traveled while providing passengers with a 20-percent fare discount, on top of existing discounts for students, senior citizens, and persons with disabilities. He added that TUPAD Tuloy-Pasada also provided additional income to public utility drivers, while commuters in Metro Manila continued to receive a 50-percent fare discount on LRT-2 and MRT-3 services. Marcos said the government likewise temporarily reduced or suspended various fees in airports, seaports, the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX), and expressways, including terminal fees, harbor charges, toll fees, and Ro-Ro terminal charges for agricultural cargo to lower transport costs and help keep food prices stable. Continuing support President Marcos acknowledged that the effects of the conflict remain despite the government's interventions, saying five months after the war began, Filipinos continue to feel its economic impact. "Hangga’t kailangan, asahan ninyo na hindi titigil ang pagsuporta ng pamahalaan (For as long as necessary, you can expect that the government will not stop supporting you),” he said. The President said the administration has allocated more than P60 billion for continuing interventions until the end of the year, adding that funds recovered from corrupt officials would instead be used to help the people. Marcos said the government will focus assistance on 3.5 million beneficiaries of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) and Walang Gutom Program, 1.5 million minimum-wage earners who are Social Security System (SSS) members, 2.5 million poor Filipinos who have yet to receive government aid, as well as the transport, agriculture, and OFW sectors affected by the conflict. "Kung susumahin, mahigit pito't kalahating milyong pamilya na lubos na nangangailangan ang matutulungan natin sa mabigat na kabanatang ito (All told, more than 7.5 million families most in need will receive assistance during this difficult chapter),” he said.

Abandoned van yields P14-M smuggled cigarettes. ZAMBOANGA CITY – Smuggled cigarettes were recovered in an abandoned van in Barangay Campo Islam here over the weekend. Police said the contraband was left behind by men who sensed their presence while transporting the illicit cargo. Discovered were 651 master cases and 715 reams of imported cigarettes valued at approximately P14 million. These were inventoried and turned over to the Bureau of Customs for proper disposition. Units involved in the operation were the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group-9, Zamboanga City Police Station 11, and the Bureau of Customs.

ASF infects 300 hogs in Lamitan City. ZAMBOANGA CITY – African Swine Fever has infected 284 hogs in Lamitan City, Basilan. The Lamitan City Veterinary Office said they are looking at this city as the possible source of the disease following an infection of hogs in Barangay Calugusan, the first barangay where ASF was detected. Hogs from the area were sourced from Zamboanga City where ASF cases were recently confirmed. Zamboanga City has strengthened border control to contain the spread of ASF. The Lamitan City Veterinary Office has intensified surveillance and monitoring activities to control the spread of the disease. Authorities appealed to Lamitan residents to report any suspected cases to the City Veterinary Office. Pigs from 113 hog raisers in Lamitan were said to be affected.

'Hindi kasalanan ng consumer': Marcos wants systems loss charges removed from electric bills. President Marcos on Monday called on Congress to immediately amend the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA), saying consumers should no longer shoulder systems loss charges in their electricity bills because these are not their responsibility. The announcement, made during his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA) on Monday, July 27, earned the longest round of applause and standing ovation from those present at Batasang Pambansa. "At kung pagbawas ng presyo ang usapan, sa aking palagay, panahon na para tanggalin na ang systems loss na ipinapasa sa consumer (And if we are talking about lowering prices, I believe it is time to remove the systems loss charge that is being passed on to consumers),” he said. "Hindi naman kasalanan ng consumer kung bakit nagkaroon ng systems loss. Kaya hindi naman tama na sila pa ang pagbabayarin dito (The systems loss is not the consumer's fault. It is therefore not right that they should be made to pay for it),” he added. With this, the President said the EPIRA should be amended immediately. "Therefore, we, the people, request—no, we demand—for the immediate amendment of the EPIRA and to prohibit charging systems loss against consumers, including the value added tax thereon," he said, EPIRA, or Republic Act No. 9136, restructured and privatized the country's electric power industry in 2001 to promote competition, encourage private investment, and improve the efficiency of electricity generation, transmission, and distribution. Under existing regulations implementing EPIRA, distribution utilities are allowed to recover a portion of systems loss—the electricity lost during transmission and distribution because of technical losses and, within regulatory limits, non-technical losses such as pilferage—from consumers through a systems loss charge reflected in monthly electricity bills. Marcos argued that removing the charge from consumers' bills would help reduce electricity costs by shifting the burden away from households and businesses, making an amendment to the law necessary. 'Sariling Kuryente' Act Alongside the proposed EPIRA amendment, President Marcos appealed to lawmakers to pass the proposed "Sariling Kuryente" Act to make it easier and more affordable for households to install rooftop solar panels and battery storage systems. "Upang maging simple, madali, at abot-kaya ang pagpapakabit ng solar panels at battery storage system sa kanilang mga bahay, hinihiling ko ang tulong ng Kongreso para maipasa ang 'Sariling Kuryente' Act (To make the installation of solar panels and battery storage systems in homes simple, easy, and affordable, I ask Congress to pass the 'Sariling Kuryente' Act),” he said. Expanding power capacity The President said the administration is closely monitoring around 200 energy projects scheduled for completion before the end of his term, with a combined capacity of nearly 10,000 megawatts. He said 45 projects have already been completed, 31 are expected to come online this year, and another 124 are targeted for completion by 2028. Marcos added that the government is also developing energy storage projects capable of delivering more than 1,700 megawatts, which he said would provide additional energy security for nearly 30 million households and industries by 2028. He attributed the faster rollout of the projects to policy and regulatory reforms designed to make it easier for both local and foreign investors to do business in the country. Renewable and indigenous energy Marcos said the administration continues to prioritize energy technologies that reduce dependence on imported oil by maximizing the country's indigenous and renewable energy resources. "Bukod sa ilang mga plantang pinapatakbo ng krudo, nakapagdagdag tayo ng mahigit animnapung plantang pinapatakbo naman ng geothermal, solar, hydro, wind, at biomass (Aside from several oil-fired power plants, we have added more than 60 power plants powered by geothermal, solar, hydro, wind, and biomass),” he said. The President also cited the extension of the Malampaya service contract until 2039, which allowed drilling to resume for the first time in eight years. "What we have uncovered is truly a national treasure: an untapped reserve of 222 billion cubic feet of natural gas, which bodes well for the continuous production of our premier gas field until 2034," he said. Marcos noted that the newly discovered reserve is enough to supply electricity to about 1.6 million households for the next eight years. He also announced that the government has awarded 14 petroleum service contracts across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao, the highest number issued during a single presidential term. Four of the contracts involve hydrogen production, which he described as a clean fuel that could serve as backup power for generating plants, particularly in off-grid areas. The President added that two petroleum service contracts are being jointly managed with the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) government, marking the first such arrangement in the country's history and supporting the region's goal of achieving energy security and full electrification. Nuclear option revisited The Chief Executive said the government has begun developing hydrogen power plants in Marinduque, Masbate, Zamboanga Sibugay, Basilan, and other potential sites as part of its long-term energy strategy. He also renewed his call to revisit nuclear power generation, saying the technology could help reinforce the country's energy security while reducing electricity costs. "Pushing the envelope further, perhaps it is time for us to revisit nuclear energy production," Marcos said. "We are confident in its capacity to reinforce our energy security and bring down the cost of electricity in our country," he added. The President vowed that the government will ensure that the public fully understands the benefits that nuclear energy can bring to our country.

Vena Energy closes $310-million financing for Pangasinan solar hub. Renewable energy (RE) firm Vena Energy has reached financial close on a $310-million financing package for its 500-megawatt-peak (MWp) Ixus Bugallon solar power project, paving the way for construction of the facility and expanding its solar portfolio in Pangasinan province to about one gigawatt-peak (GWp). In a statement on Monday, July 27, Vena Energy said the project had reached financial close, marking a key milestone before construction begins. The project, which was awarded under the second round of the Green Energy Auction (GEA-2), will be located adjacent to the company’s 550-MWp Bugallon solar power project. According to the company, the facility is expected to generate enough electricity to power approximately 650,000 households while avoiding 570,000 metric tons (MT) of carbon emissions annually. Simone Grasso, Vena Group’s chief investment officer (CIO), said the financial close would enable the company to support the country’s clean energy goals. “Achieving financial close for the Ixus Bugallon solar power project reflects the continued confidence of our banking partners in Vena Energy’s ability to develop, finance and deliver large-scale renewable energy infrastructure,” Grasso said. A syndicate of eight global financial institutions provided the $310 million, or around ₱19 billion, in senior debt financing: BNP Paribas, Crédit Agricole CIB, DBS Bank, ING, Intesa Sanpaolo, MUFG, Standard Chartered, and SMBC. The company said the successful deal reflects strong international lender confidence in Vena Energy’s project pipeline and underscores the growing global appetite for Philippine green energy investments. At present, Vena Energy has about 30.5 gigawatts (GW) of onshore wind, solar, and offshore wind projects, as well as 26.2 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery energy storage systems (BESS) and 848 kilotons per annum (KTPA) of green hydrogen and ammonia. - Gabriell Christel Galang

Say Alonzo mourns loss after fire razes restaurant she worked hard to build. Say Alonzo is asking for prayers after a fire destroyed her restaurant in Laguna. The “Pinoy Big Brother” alum shared details of the unfortunate incident on Instagram on Sunday, July 26, posting footage of her food business, which she opened in 2024, engulfed in thick smoke. "Thank you to everyone who’ve sent prayers and messages. It’s really hard to accept what happened but we have no choice but to move on and plan what we will do next," Say wrote in her post. Say also wrote in her post that she is not ready to see the property after what happened; she and her husband Ryan Tordesillas could not sleep because of the loss. "I’ve only seen the videos from the news—each video made me cry, and those videos are still making me cry. After Sunday Mass, we usually pass by for inasal take-out, but today, it was different. I cried in Mass, and the kids told me if we could please not pass by the restaurant because they don’t want to see it. Ryan and I don’t want to see it either. It’s like seeing your hard-earned money and dreams burned,” she stated. Despite what happened, Say hopes and prays that they will recover and rise again. "Don’t you worry, we will be back stronger! When that time comes, I hope all of you will still be here to support us. For the meantime, please pray for us. Hope things will be better for us soon!" Say said.

IT'S OFFICIAL: Alyssa Valdez confirms relationship with golfer. Alyssa Valdez made it official, and her fans couldn't be happier for "The Phenom". The 33-year-old Valdez confirmed her relationship with Ian Umali, a golfer and businessman, on Instagram recently. “Hi guys! So, we’re here at MiraNamin celebrating my birthday and my boyfriend’s birthday, Ian,” Valdez said. There, Valdez asked some of her friends what they wanted to manifest for her this year, sparking plenty of "kilig" as several of them hinted at the Alas Pilipinas star finally receiving a marriage proposal. “Proposal,” said beauty queen and TV personality Samantha Bernardo, who also hopes Valdez will have more time for herself and venture into other things in coaching or writing a book. “Ano ba!” Valdez responded. Actress Angelica Panganiban also teased Valdez about getting an engagement ring. “Nakuha mo na lahat ng trophies na kailangan mo sa buhay mo, ang ima-manifest ko ‘yong kaya mong isuot araw-araw… sa daliri,” said Panganiban. But the highlight of the 2-minute video was when Ian gave his answers. “We just had meetings about it this year, di ba?” said Ian, who ended his piece with a kiss on Alyssa’s cheek. “We’re planning something big, something to organize, and be intentional about what she wants to do in the future. So ‘yon that’s the one.” The decorated spiker, who captained Alas in the AVC Women's Volleyball Cup in Candon City last month, is still playing for the Creamline Cool Smashers in the Premier Volleyball League (PVL).

PBBM calls for whole-of-society effort to protect children from online harms. President Marcos has called on all sectors of society to work together to protect Filipino children from the harmful effects of fake news, pornography, violent content, and toxic social media, saying these have contributed to worsening mental health issues, teenage pregnancies, HIV/AIDS cases, and other social problems. Marcos said this following the series of school violence that resulted in injuries and deaths of students in the country in recent months. In his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA) on Monday, July 27, the President warned that "pernicious influences" have led to issues of mental health, the rise in teenage pregnancies and HIV/AIDS cases, and other extremely harmful consequences. "We must protect them from the harmful influences and forces that exploit their vulnerability: the corrosive influence of fake news; the unfettered exposure to pornography, even to minors; the constant depiction of casual violence; and the toxicity and hate culture pervasive in social media," he said. "We must all assume a community responsibility for our young people's protection," he added. The President said schools must become safe spaces where children are protected and nurtured. "Tatayo ang paaralan bilang pangalawang tahanan para sa kanila. Kaya hinahanda natin ang mga pampublikong paaralan upang tanggapin sila nang bukas-palad (Schools will stand as their second home. That is why we are preparing our public schools to welcome them with open arms),” he added. Whole-of-society responsibility Marcos said protecting children requires the participation not only of government but also of families, schools, churches, industries, and communities. "Kailangang mamulat ang buong lipunan at akuin ang responsibilidad. Pag-ibayuhin natin ang ating paggabay at pag-aruga sa ating kabataan (The whole of society must awaken and assume this responsibility. Let us strengthen our guidance and care for our youth),” he said. "Magkakasama tayong lahat sa misyong ito: ang pamahalaan, pamilya, paaralan, simbahan, industriya, at komunidad (We are all together in this mission: the government, the family, the schools, the Church, industry, and the community),” he added. Remembering slain students President Marcos said the recent deaths of several students due to violence and negligence should serve as a painful reminder of the country's collective responsibility to safeguard the youth. "Ang mga nasawi nating mga mag-aaral kamakailan dala ng karahasan at kapabayaan ay nag-iwan ng malaking puwang sa kanilang pamilya at mapait na aral din para sa ating lahat (The students we recently lost because of violence and negligence have left a huge void in their families and a bitter lesson for all of us),” he said. "Sa mga magulang at kaanak ng mga nasawi at nasaktan dahil sa nangyaring karahasan sa mga paaralan, tanggapin po ninyo ang aming taimtim na pakikiramay (To the parents and relatives of those who died and were injured because of violence in our schools, please accept our deepest condolences),” he added. Addressing the families of Chris Lorenz Fabian, Joyancee Separa, and Ayessa Nicole Dazo, Marcos said their children demonstrated courage and selflessness that should inspire all Filipinos. "We are all so very proud of the unflinching bravery and heroic virtue that you have instilled in your children," he said. "Their courage and selflessness — true Filipino qualities — are the virtues that these trying times call for," he added. It can be recalled that in June, President Marcos directed the Departments of Education (DepEd), Interior and Local Government (DILG), Health (DOH), and the Philippine National Police (PNP) to strengthen measures to ensure the safety of students following a series of violent incidents and accidents involving young Filipinos. He said schools should remain places of learning rather than fear, urged parents and teachers to play a more active role in protecting children, and reminded students that seeking help is "never a sign of weakness" as investigations continue into recent incidents, including possible cases of bullying.

Bargain hunters lift PSEi as oil prices tumble. The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) rose on Monday, July 27, after the halt in hostilities in the Middle East prompted some investors to start bargain-hunting. The main index gained 33.89 points, or 0.54 percent, to close at 6,314.90. Miners led the advance, while conglomerates and industrials lagged behind. Volume declined to 448 million shares worth ₱4.81 billion. Gainers outnumbered losers—94 to 75, with 67 issues unchanged. “The local bourse ended higher as bargain hunting persisted during the session amid easing geopolitical tensions following a strike halt in the Middle East,” said Regina Capital Development Corp. managing director Luis Limlingan. Investor sentiment was further supported by the sharp decline in crude oil prices, which helped ease concerns over inflationary pressures. Market participants remained cautiously optimistic as lower oil prices provided some relief to the broader market. Rizal Commercial Banking Corp.
